items.title: Don’t turn churches into campaign arena, Soludo cautions politicians
items.description: By Vincent Ujumadu Governor Charles Soludo of Anambra State, on Sunday, cautioned politicians against turning churches and other places of worship into a political arena, stating that sacred spaces must remain neutral grounds for people of all political persuasions. Soludo made the remark during the 30th anniversary celebration of the Mountain of Holy Ghost Intervention and Deliverance Ministry founded by Prophet Chukwuemeka Ohanaemere, popularly known as Odumeje. Addressing the congregation, the governor stressed the need for the men of God to clearly separate politics from worship. According to Soludo, the place of worship should be a holy place where people of all political persuasion should come and worship God in peace. “It should not be a place for politics. There is a venue for politics. If you want to worship God, you have to go to the house of God. We must separate the two things clearly,” Soludo said. He recalled that six months before his election, he took a deliberate decision never to go to any church to cup a microphone to ask them to vote for him or to campaign. “It was a deliberate decision. I worshipped in the government house chapel until the election day and afterwards,” the governor stated. “We must never politicise the church. We must never politicise the place of worship. Politicians, keep off churches. Keep off places of worship. That’s a deliberate message, and it is my kind of consistency of character”, he further said. items.title: 3rd US aircraft carrier arrives in Middle East amid Iran tensions
items.description: The USS Theodore Roosevelt aircraft carrier has arrived in the Middle East, bringing the number of US carrier strike groups in the region to three amid continued tensions with Iran, a US official confirmed on Monday. The carrier arrived in the area of responsibility of the US Central Command on Sunday, according to US media outlets. It joins the USS George H.W. Bush and the USS George Washington, which have been deployed in the region since April and August, respectively. The US Navy's presence in the Arabian Sea now includes three aircraft carriers, 13 destroyers, two cruisers and a littoral combat ship, according to US media reports. The deployment comes as diplomatic efforts between Washington and Tehran remain stalled and US President Donald Trump is considering whether to resume large-scale military strikes against Iran. On February 28, Israel and the United States launched joint attacks on Tehran and other Iranian cities. Iran responded with waves of missile and drone strikes targeting Israel and US bases and assets in the region, while tightening its control over the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Waste Crisis: Lagos trains sanitation workers on safety
items.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State Government has reaffirmed its commitment to improving the capacity, efficiency and professionalism of sanitation workers as part of efforts to address the state’s waste management challenges and ensure a cleaner environment. The government gave the assurance on Monday at a capacity-building workshop for selected sanitation workers held in Alausa, Ikeja. The Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Omobolaji Gaji, represented by the Director of Sanitation Services, Dr Hassan Sanuth, said the workshop was designed to equip participants with the knowledge, practical skills and safety measures required to improve sanitation operations. He said the initiative was also aimed at promoting a cleaner, healthier and more sustainable Lagos. Gaji described sanitation workers as indispensable partners in the state’s efforts to maintain a clean and liveable environment, noting that their daily responsibilities, including street sweeping, drainage clearing and waste collection, were critical to protecting public health and preventing flooding. He commended the workers for their dedication, observing that many of them commence their duties early in the morning, long before most residents begin their daily activities. According to him, their contributions remain essential to maintaining environmental orderliness and ensuring that Lagos remains a city residents can be proud of. The Permanent Secretary explained that the selected workers were identified in recognition of their commitment and dedication to duty, adding that the training represented a deliberate government investment in improving their welfare, competence and productivity. He said participants would be exposed to safer working practices, the appropriate use of personal protective equipment, modern waste-handling techniques and improved approaches to sanitation service delivery. Gaji added that the workshop would provide an opportunity for the workers to exchange experiences, discuss challenges encountered in the field and learn from one another. He urged participants to actively engage with facilitators, ask questions and contribute ideas that could enhance their professional capacity and performance. “This capacity-building programme underscores the Lagos State Government’s commitment to developing a more skilled, safety-conscious and efficient sanitation workforce capable of responding effectively to the environmental challenges of a rapidly growing metropolis,” he said. He also appreciated the facilitators, partners and stakeholders whose expertise and support contributed to the programme, urging continued collaboration to strengthen environmental sanitation and public health in the state. Gaji said a clean and sustainable Lagos required collective responsibility, stressing that sanitation workers remained at the centre of the state’s environmental management efforts. He assured the workers that their contributions were valued, their dignity respected and their professional development remained important to the government. In a lecture titled, “Safety Culture: A Need to Prevent Occupational Accidents,” the guest lecturer, Mr Adeyinka Adebiyi, urged sanitation workers to prioritise workplace safety in the discharge of their daily responsibilities. Adebiyi noted that their duties exposed them to various occupational hazards capable of causing injuries, illnesses and, in severe cases, loss of lives. He emphasised the need for strict compliance with safety procedures, proper use of personal protective equipment, effective risk assessment and responsible handling of waste materials. He also urged the workers to remain vigilant, avoid unsafe practices and promptly report potential hazards to prevent avoidable accidents and health complications. The capacity-building initiative is expected to improve sanitation service delivery, promote safer working conditions and contribute to a cleaner environment across Lagos State. items.title: Customers report service outages at major US banks
items.description: Thousands of customers at major US banks, including JP Morgan Chase, Wells Fargo and Bank of America, have reported trouble accessing services. Chase Bank – the largest banking institution in the US – said a “software bug” in its hardware systems may have been behind the glitch and noted the impacts may have affected other banks. It added the issue was “temporary” and not “systemic” or “cyber-related”. Problems appeared to be easing for many customers by early Monday evening. The issue comes after a string of unrelated technical problems last week, including a massive Microsoft outage, as well as a telecommunications issue and network failure that grounded all US flights. Problems started throughout the afternoon on Monday. There were almost 5,000 reports of Chase Bank’s services being down, according to the Downdetector website. Chase Bank told it’s customers that “some transactions are taking longer than usual to complete” but they still had “access to their accounts and funds”. The bank, a subsidiary of JP Morgan Chase, serves more than 86m customers at 5,000 branches across the US, as well as 7.4m small businesses, according to the company’s webpage. It is also the top credit card issuer in the US. The exact nature of the bug was unclear. The BBC has contacted Chase Bank. Another institution, US Bank, said some its systems were not directly affected but clients using the Zelle, a digital payment platform, received error messages saying their payments could not be sent. Zelle has said its service is “operating as it should” and issues at other banks could be affecting payments. Customers also reported issues with Truist, PNC and Capital One but all these companies told the BBC they have not been impacted. As of 1800 ET (2300G), Chase, Bank of America and US Bank had seen a fall in the number of reported outages.

items.title: Five EU countries announce migrant deportation centre in Rwanda
items.description: Five EU countries will open a migrant deportation centre in Rwanda next year as part of a broader push to boost removals. Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands are expected to open a “return hub” ready to accept transfers in 2027, the Dutch and Danish governments announced in statements. The countries said the scheme would apply to migrants staying illegally in their nations who are subject to deportation, with the Dutch government adding it will provide an alternative if deportees cannot be returned to their country of origin. Deportees will be able to either integrate into Rwandan society or return to their home country, the nations said. The scheme will apply to people who have exhausted their legal avenues to stay in the five nations – unlike a scrapped British deal that envisaged sending people to Rwanda to have their claims processed. Legal challenges meant the UK deal never took off, and it was eventually junked by the incoming Labour government in 2024 . Downing Street has not ruled out the UK joining the scheme, saying they will watch it “with interest”. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said the plan to open a centre in Rwanda had no “future or humanity”, according to AFP news agency. “I don’t see any future or humanity in that. It’s not the solution,” Sanchez told the Spanish broadcaster Telecinco, AFP reported. The five countries say the plan to send migrants abroad is in line with EU and international law, but human rights bodies say it could violate migrant rights. The deal follows a recent EU reform that allowed for the creation of hubs outside of the bloc. In a joint press conference in Vienna on Monday, Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker said the five countries wanted to relieve European asylum systems and stop traffickers arranging deadly trips across the Mediterranean. In a written statement, the Dutch government said the five countries will “only return single men” as part of the first phase of the deal, adding that the focus for the Netherlands “will be on persons from countries of origin in the same region as Rwanda”. Once in Rwanda, people will be able to integrate into society, which means they will have the right of residence, as well as access to education, healthcare, the labour market and the legal system. Rwandan Interior Minister Vincent Biruta said the country is commmited to working with European partners to provide a “safe, legal and dignified solution for migrants”. He added that they would also work on “correcting the global imbalance in economic opportunities”, which he called a “key driver of irregular migration”. The United Nations’ International Organisation for Migration (IOM) could play an ancillary role. “IOM has a long history of providing assistance to migrants in situations of transit, including in complex contexts,” an IOM spokesperson said, adding the agency was in discussions with some EU countries “on plans for the establishment of return hubs or similar mechanisms”. With elections approaching in several EU nations, administrations have been under pressure to show they can control migration. Concerns around security, struggling economies and disillusionment with governing parties have all had a major role in shaping attitudes towards people leaving their home countries . Human Rights Watch’s senior Africa researcher Clementine de Montjoye said the choice of Rwanda would bea cause of concern as it had a “well-established record of repression of dissent, arbitrary detention, ill-treatment in detention” and support for armed rebels in the neighbouring Democratic Republic of Congo. “Paying Kigali to host a deportation programme would not only cause suffering and harm to those deported, it would finance and provide political leverage to a government responsible for serious human rights abuses at home and abroad.” The independent EU Agency for Fundamental Rights argued any third country hosting a return hub should “respect fundamental rights”, including that people should not be sent to a country where they face serious risk of persecution. The agency added that unaccompanied children should not be sent to a return hub, which the Dutch government has confirmed will not take place. According to the European Border and Coast Guard Agency, there were almost 110,000 irregular border crossings into the EU in the first 10 months of 2026, which represents a 29% decrease compared to the previous year. In October, about 18,100 crossings were detected, which is about 6% less than October 2025 but 22% more than in September “largely because of a sharp rise in arrivals on the Western African route to the Canary Islands”.

items.title: MINURSO : la mission onusienne entame son retrait du Sahara après 35 ans
items.description: Un premier groupe de cinq membres de la composante militaire de la Mission des Nations unies pour l’organisation d’un référendum au Sahara (MINURSO) a quitté lundi soir Laâyoune, marquant le début du processus de retrait des personnels de la mission de la région. Les cinq militaires ont quitté le territoire via l’aéroport Hassan Ier de Laâyoune, dans le cadre d’une opération qui devrait se poursuivre au cours des prochains jours, selon des sources citées par Hespress. Cette première étape intervient après la décision du Conseil de sécurité de ne pas renouveler le mandat de la MINURSO, arrivé à expiration le 31 octobre dernier. Depuis le 1er novembre, la mission est ainsi entrée dans une phase de liquidation progressive de ses opérations, après plus de 35 ans de présence sur le terrain. Selon les éléments communiqués par les Nations unies, le processus de liquidation doit s’effectuer progressivement. Il prévoit notamment le rapatriement d’environ 160 observateurs militaires, ainsi que la réduction des effectifs civils et des personnels associés à la mission. La procédure doit également inclure la fermeture et la remise de plusieurs sites et installations utilisés par la MINURSO, ainsi que la gestion de ses équipements et biens. Les Nations unies prévoient par ailleurs la fin progressive des dispositifs de communication et de soutien logistique, la gestion des archives et des dossiers de la mission, ainsi que le règlement des contrats et engagements liés à sa présence sur le terrain. Cette opération est supervisée par une équipe réduite relevant du Département de l’appui opérationnel des Nations unies, sous la conduite d’Alexander Ivanko, ancien chef de la MINURSO et représentant spécial de l’ONU dans la région. Une nouvelle étape après la fin du mandat Cette évolution fait suite aux développements intervenus après la décision du Conseil de sécurité de ne pas renouveler le mandat de la mission lors de sa réunion du 30 octobre. Le 4 novembre, le roi Mohammed VI avait présidé au Palais Royal de Rabat une séance de travail consacrée au suivi de la période post-MINURSO et aux dispositions à mettre en œuvre après la fin du mandat de la mission. L’ONU avait, de son côté, confirmé que le 1er novembre marquait le début de la période consacrée à la liquidation de la mission. L’ONU maintient son engagement politique La fin des opérations de terrain de la MINURSO ne signifie toutefois pas, selon les Nations unies, l’abandon du processus politique relatif au dossier du Sahara. Le secrétaire général de l’ONU, António Guterres, a souligné que l’organisation internationale restait disposée à accompagner les parties dans la recherche d’une solution politique, notamment à travers son envoyé personnel pour le Sahara, Staffan de Mistura. Le départ de ce premier groupe de cinq militaires constitue ainsi la première manifestation concrète sur le terrain du processus de retrait annoncé par les Nations unies. Les autres départs et la fermeture progressive des installations doivent se poursuivre conformément au calendrier établi pour la liquidation de la mission. items.title: Bangladesh: Education Crisis for Rohingya Refugee Children
items.description: Click to expand Image A learning center in a Cox’s Bazar refugee camp in Bangladesh, September 17, 2026. © 2026 Private (Bangkok) – Humanitarian education programs for Rohingya refugee children in Bangladesh are struggling amid a collapse in donor funding, Human Rights Watch said today. Donors should fully fund the education programs, while Bangladesh should recognize and the United Nations should support a separate Rohingya-led school network. Humanitarian education programs have enrolled 312,000 out of approximately 500,000 school-age Rohingya children in the Bangladesh refugee camps. But the programs, which aid cuts had shuttered for months in 2025, are barely adequate even for the children they reach and may close again, humanitarian officials told Human Rights Watch. While resources are shrinking, about 90,000 more refugee children need schooling this year, due to population growth and new arrivals fleeing atrocities in Myanmar. The donor-supported programs have largely ignored the schools that Rohingya teachers set up in the camps, which are well-regarded by refugees for their quality of education, but lack legal status and reach only about 30,000 students. “Donor governments have turned their backs on education for half a million Rohingya students stuck in the world’s largest refugee camp, but so much could be done to mitigate this crisis,” said Bill Van Esveld, associate children’s rights director at Human Rights Watch. “Bangladesh should accelerate steps to end bans on education for refugees, and humanitarian agencies should work with the Rohingya-led schools.” On November 19, 2026, the International Court of Justice will deliver its judgment in the case brought by Gambia alleging that Myanmar’s atrocities against the Rohingya during the 2016-2017 “clearance operations” constitute genocide and violate the Genocide Convention. Bangladesh’s Awami League government, overthrown in 2024, had banned Rohingya children’s access to certified education and higher education in the camps or in the Bangladesh school system. It allowed donor-funded education programs but prohibited Rohingya community-led schools, demolished several, and threatened teachers with exile to Bhasan Char, a remote island. The current government has taken positive steps and should lift remaining restrictions on refugees’ access to education amid the donor funding crisis, Human Rights Watch said. In October, Bangladesh for the first time allowed a few dozen Rohingya primary students to take an internationally recognized primary school examination, supported by the UN High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR). Also for the first time, Bangladesh in October approved a Rohingya nongovernmental organization’s plans to build a primary school in the camps for 240 students and to provide a structured curriculum. The Rohingya Centre UK, set up by the diaspora Rohingya community, said that the 10-subject curriculum will be taught from 9 a.m. to 3 p.m., significantly more instruction than students receive in donor-funded education programs. The organization is also running training on the new curriculum for other Rohingya-led schools in the camps. Teachers in the camps established the Examination Board of Rohingya Refugees in 2025, which now comprises more than 125 community-led schools with up to 30,000 students, and is working to ensure quality education, including standardized exams in the Myanmar curriculum. Establishing the examination board took a year of volunteer outreach in the camps. However, the Bangladesh government has still not accredited any curriculum for Rohingya children, and because community-led schools lack legal status, they cannot receive foreign support directly. As a result, while the UK organization’s school is able to hire and train Rohingya teachers, the project is formally being implemented through a registered Bangladeshi group. Most community-led schools have to charge students small fees to operate, limiting access, and rely on refugees to donate the use of their small living shelters as makeshift classrooms. Eight teachers at community-led schools said that to reach more students, they need Bangladesh to grant their schools official status, allow official certification of education and a pathway to higher education, and for the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) and humanitarian organizations to acknowledge their work and engage with them. A teacher at one of the schools said, “We are spending money to ensure education quality, as if we were a government, but we are not a government, we are simply refugees.” Leaders and teachers offered to collaborate with UNICEF and humanitarian organizations on examinations, quality assurance, and improved teaching. The vast majority of Rohingya students rely on donor-funded humanitarian education programs. Humanitarian groups providing education, coordinated by UNICEF, received just US$29 million from donors towards their 2025 budget request of $72 million, resulting in “learning centers” in the refugee camps closing for months. The education sector laid off teachers, cancelled an early education program, and cut teacher trainings and other programs. In October 2026, a humanitarian education official told Human Rights Watch: “We are struggling to maintain the most basic services. Even textbooks are [insufficient].… We cannot ensure children receive materials like a pencil, a notebook.... Learning centers were damaged by mudslides and climate events, but we do not have funding to carry out repairs.” Several Rohingya instructors at learning centers that rely on humanitarian funds confirmed the lack of resources. A grade 1 instructor said his classroom had no whiteboard, markers, desks, or benches, and students had to share textbooks, pens, and exercise books. A grade 3 instructor worried that “three students are using one set of textbooks.” Rather than teaching one class for the full school day, learning center instructors teach students in two “shifts” per day. Even after humanitarian agencies reduced their education funding request to $53 million for 2026, donors had pledged only $36 million by mid-October, leaving learning centers at risk of closing again, humanitarian officials said. The World Bank and Education Cannot Wait have provided or pledged funding, but this alone is insufficient. The United States had paid for half the Rohingya education budget before halting its funding in 2025. Globally, humanitarian education funding has fallen by 20 percent since 2023. All states are obligated to provide children access to quality education without discrimination, regardless of their refugee status. The Inter-Agency Network for Education in Emergencies’ Minimum Standards emphasize the importance of community leadership and participation in the design and implementation of education programming. “Rohingya children are eager to learn,” said a Rohingya teacher in the camps. “The problem is that their education has been repeatedly interrupted by circumstances beyond their control. Education needs to be treated as a right, not a temporary humanitarian project.”

items.title: Éducation : le gouvernement promet de solder les engagements du dialogue social d’ici début 2027
items.description: Le ministre de l’Éducation nationale, du Préscolaire, de la Formation professionnelle et de la Qualification, Nabil Benabdallah, a annoncé lundi à Rabat que l’ensemble des engagements encore en suspens issus de l’accord du dialogue social de 2023 devraient être mis en œuvre dans les prochaines semaines, et au plus tard au début de 2027. Répondant à une question centrale sur le dialogue social dans le secteur de l’éducation nationale à la Chambre des représentants, le ministre a assuré que son département entend accélérer la mise en œuvre des dispositions de l’accord qui n’ont pas encore été concrétisées. Pour Nabil Benabdallah, le dialogue social et les échanges réguliers avec les syndicats constituent un axe essentiel de l’action du ministère. Il a estimé que la prise en compte des attentes exprimées dans ce cadre est nécessaire pour mobiliser pleinement les personnels de l’éducation nationale et de la formation professionnelle. Le ministre a également fait état d’échanges informels quotidiens avec les organisations syndicales, avec pour objectif de maintenir un climat favorable au bon déroulement de l’année scolaire et d’éviter le retour de tensions susceptibles de compliquer les chantiers de réforme. 17 milliards de dirhams supplémentaires Concernant les engagements de l’accord de 2023, le ministre a indiqué que leur mise en œuvre, dans leur état actuel et sans intégrer les éventuels ajustements nécessaires à certaines situations, nécessiterait près de 17 milliards de dirhams supplémentaires par rapport au budget initialement prévu. Il a par ailleurs évoqué le statut des fonctionnaires de l’Éducation nationale, dont certaines dispositions peuvent, selon lui, entrer en contradiction ou répondre à des intérêts divergents entre différentes catégories de personnels. Le ministre a expliqué que cette situation était notamment liée aux contraintes de la conjoncture et à la nécessité de préserver la paix sociale. Il a ainsi confirmé que cette question sera soumise au dialogue social afin de parvenir à une issue consensuelle. 63 textes pour achever la réforme du statut S’agissant de la finalisation du statut des fonctionnaires de l’Éducation nationale, Nabil Benabdallah a indiqué que le processus législatif et réglementaire porte sur 63 textes, dont 46 ont déjà été approuvés. Les textes restants devraient être soumis à la procédure d’approbation au cours des prochaines semaines, a-t-il précisé. Le ministre a également rappelé les conclusions du dialogue consacré à la formation professionnelle les 23 et 24 octobre 2025. Celui-ci avait notamment porté sur la formation continue, les prestations sociales, les indemnités, les mutations, la mobilité du personnel et les autorisations de participation aux concours professionnels, ainsi que sur la communication, les mécanismes de gestion et les ressources humaines. Vers une inspection des concours de recrutement Autre annonce : le ministère lancera une opération d’inspection consacrée aux concours de recrutement organisés dans le secteur afin de vérifier leur régularité. Nabil Benabdallah a assuré que toutes les mesures nécessaires seront prises pour garantir une transparence totale lors des prochains concours. Ces derniers devraient permettre le recrutement d’environ 20.000 nouveaux agents dans différentes catégories, avec pour objectif de préserver le principe d’égalité des chances consacré par la Constitution. À travers l’accélération de la mise en œuvre de l’accord de 2023, la poursuite du dialogue avec les syndicats et le contrôle des procédures de recrutement, le ministère entend ainsi avancer sur plusieurs dossiers qui restent au cœur des revendications du secteur. items.title: Obi, Kwankwaso have God’s grace to dislodge Tinubu — Babachir Lawal
items.description: A chieftain of Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Babachir Lawal, has said Peter Obi, the party’s presidential candidate, and Rabiu Kwankwaso, his running mate, have God’s backing to defeat President Bola Tinubu in 2027. Lawal, a former Secretary to the Government of the Federation, SGF, who made the declaration during an appearance on Arise Television late Sunday, cited the “widespread support” Obi and Kwankwaso enjoyed as a pointer to God’s grace upon their lives. He said: “I have told everybody that talks to me that both Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso have the grace of God upon their lives, which makes people like them. “The population likes them. They just show up in the market. They don’t hire people to come to their rallies. People just turn out at their own expense.” He said his experience in politics had enabled him to recognise signs that could favour the opposition alliance, adding that he previously occupied a similar position during the Muhammadu Buhari administration. “It’s not the first time I am in the position I am in now in politics. I have been in this position during Buhari’s time. Even this your president, I drove his system up to the primaries. “So I am a very skilled and experienced person in the game. I can see the signs and we know the loopholes. And we are working on the loopholes,’’ he said. Lawal expressed confidence that the NDC would defeat the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC. , saying the party had established structures and systems to achieve its objective. “We have an inside chance of toppling this government. We are inside and we know we will beat this government. “We know they are gone. We have put up structures and systems. I am 100 per cent confident,’’ he said. Lawal added that the responsibility of the party’s technical team was to convert the popularity of its presidential candidates into electoral success by ensuring that votes were protected and counted. “This grace that God has bestowed upon them, it’s our duty, the technical people, to harmonise and crystallise this thing into delivering it at the polling station and protecting the votes and ensuring it’s counted,” he said. Lawal dismissed concerns over recent departure of Yunusa Tanko, former national coordinator of the Obidient Movement; Nana Kazaure, Doyin Okupe, and the former NDC’s deputy national publicity secretary, from Obi’s camp, saying politicians were free to leave parties when their expectations were not met. He compared the development with the exit of some politicians from Tinubu’s inner circle, including Kashim Imam and Rauf Aregbesola. “I was with Bola Tinubu, but I left. I can remember Kashim Imam; he has also left. I remember Rauf Aregbesola, who was also with Bola Tinubu. But he has left. These are big politicians. But they left Bola Tinubu. “Leaving a political party is only natural. Nigeria is like a big company with many political parties. And people come in there with their own different ideas about what they can get out of it and what they can put into it,’’ the former SGF said. He said while the majority of Nigerians joined politics to get something out of it, others participate to contribute to the system. Lawal stated: “If you are the getting-out type and you go but don’t get anything, it’s only fair you move. That is life. You cannot be static. “Moreover, the Obidient system is not about money. And people have families to feed, bills to pay. And if they join the Obidient Movement hoping to get the resources to settle these, they will be disappointed. So, it’s only fair. They have their reasons for leaving,” Recounting his experience while serving as SGF, Lawal said some politicians tended to exaggerate their contributions to political campaigns. items.title: ‘We were determined to break the eight’ – Amin Adam defends debt repayment timetable
items.description: Former Finance Minister Dr Mohammed Amin Adam has rejected claims that the previous government deliberately deferred debt repayments to 2027 and 2028 to force an NDC administration into default. Speaking to Evans Mensah on Monday, he described Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson’s position on the repayment schedule as unfortunate. Amin Adam said the debt restructuring was largely completed before the election. He questioned how the previous administration could have negotiated the terms knowing the NDC would be in office when repayments fell due. “98% of the debt restructuring had been completed before we went to the election. And so, how on earth could we know that the NDC was going to be in government at the time the repayment will be due in 2027 and 2028?” Host Evans Mensah told him that political observers saw a strong prospect of an NDC victory after the previous government’s eight years in office. But Dr Amin Adam insisted that his party had fought to retain power. “Yes, but we were determined to break the eight, and we fought the election forcefully, but we lost.” He said the government campaigned to win and continue servicing the debt. It had also begun paying some bondholders before leaving office. “So, so how on earth could we be negotiating, having in mind that when it is time for repayment, the NDC will be in government and we will deliberately defer payments to that time.” He also rejected the assessment that the repayment structure had set Ghana up for another default. Amin Adam accused the Finance Minister of taking credit for the gains from restructuring while criticising the repayment obligations. He said the exercise delivered $11 billion in debt relief. That included $5 billion cancelled by external creditors and $6 billion in debt-service savings. He attributed the reduction in the debt-to-GDP ratio to those measures. He argued that the restructuring had created fiscal room for the current government. “And so you are happy to take credit for the benefits, and when it is time for repayment, you are complaining.”

items.title: The Dangerous Idea Rubio and Hegseth Are Endorsing
items.description: This is an edition of The Atlantic Daily, a newsletter that guides you through the biggest stories of the day, helps you discover new ideas, and recommends the best in culture. Sign up for it here. When Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth was reprimanded by a sentinel last week for a lack of decorum at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, his response was unusually gracious: He promptly awarded the sentinel the Joint Service Commendation Medal. Perhaps Hegseth’s conciliatory response was not because he recognized he’d violated the sanctity of the location , but because he’d been yelled at by one authority he recognizes: a man with a gun. This thought occurred to me over the weekend, when Hegseth posted a clip of Secretary of State Marco Rubio speaking at a Federalist Society conference Friday evening. Rubio praised President Trump’s sanctions earlier this year on the International Criminal Court. So far, so normal: The right has long despised the ICC, arguing that it violates American sovereignty and could be used as a foreign-policy weapon by U.S. adversaries. Then things got strange. Rubio said that if the ICC tried to exercise jurisdiction over Americans, “our answer will probably be the same as the Roman general, Pompey, when he said to those who were trying to invoke their cities’ charters against his legions. He said, ‘Stop quoting laws to men with swords.’” This is an odd thing to say to a room full of lawyers, and it was met with some awkward chuckles. Only once Rubio declared Pompey’s statement as “not politically correct” did he win applause. But Hegseth was apparently taken with the quote and reposted it, writing , “Stop quoting laws to MEN WITH SWORDS.” Rubio and Hegseth are expressing a core view of the second Trump administration: that might makes right and rules are for sissies. In January, now–White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller explained the American quasi-colonization of Venezuela this way. “We live in a world in which you can talk all you want about international niceties and everything else, but we live in a world,” he said, “that is governed by strength, that is governed by force, that is governed by power. These are the iron laws of the world that have existed since the beginning of time.” (No wonder that the United States—with Rubio acting as viceroy—has signaled that it prefers rule by the Nicolás Maduro protégé Delcy Rodríguez to María Corina Machado’s attempts to restore democracy in the country.) Trump has shown that he prefers the performative machismo of Vladimir Putin’s Russian military to Ukraine’s legal and moral claim on its land, and he has mused publicly about actions against Iran that would be war crimes. The Trumpist fidelity to this idea is particularly true with regard to international law, but it extends to a consistent disregard for the laws of the United States as well. At the Pentagon, Hegseth has raged against rules of engagement for the military and loosened them for the war in Iran, which may be one reason that the U.S. bombed an elementary school in Iran early in the conflict. (Superior American military might has not prevailed in Iran so far, either.) The military has also killed almost 250 people in extrajudicial and likely illegal strikes on boats that American officials allege are carrying drugs. The epithet un-American is overused, but in this case, it is literally true. “The very purpose of the American founding was to ensure that force would always be subject to law, which would itself flow from natural right and popular consent,” John R. Puri writes in National Review . “That is why one of the Founders’ great innovations was to place the new U.S. armed forces under strict civilian control.” One specific complaint in the Declaration of Independence was that King George III had “affected to render the Military independent of and superior to the Civil power.” By contrast, John Adams wrote that a republic was a government “of Laws, and not of Men,” a stipulation that very much includes men with swords who might try to supersede law. Hegseth is himself now a lawless man with (metaphorical) swords, and in his enthusiastic endorsement of Rubio’s remark, we may find insight into both why Hegseth joined the Army out of college and why his career languished. Maybe he thought joining the military was a ticket to cracking heads without restriction. Instead, he found a careful, disciplined, and rule-abiding force, and he never advanced very far. As my colleague Eliot A. Cohen has written , “The Army, unlike Princeton and Harvard, knew a petulant, insecure mediocrity when it saw one.” Hegseth eventually left the National Guard when he was sidelined over concerns about extremism. As secretary, he has gone about destroying the institution that spurned him, as well as working to ensure that the people bearing swords are almost entirely men. As for Rubio, he has recently become a fount of classical references , perhaps under the influence of white-nationalist ideas circulating at the State Department. But mouthing these words is different from understanding what they mean. As a young commander during a Roman civil war in the 80s B.C.E., Pompey earned the nickname adulescentulus carnifex —“teenage butcher.” When residents of the Sicilian city of Messana resisted his authority, citing ancient Roman law, he uttered the quotation that Rubio cites. The American Founders—and indeed most Americans throughout history—would have seen themselves in the citizens of Messana, not the ruthless general. Things didn’t turn out well for Pompey. He enjoyed years of political and military success during a period when republican rule was teetering, eventually becoming part of a ruling triumvirate with Julius Caesar and Marcus Licinius Crassus. But he eventually fell out with Caesar, resulting in another civil war. Pompey fled Rome but was killed and beheaded in Egypt. Nor, more important, did Pompey’s era end well for the Roman Republic. When the long-running political crisis that spawned both civil wars was over, the republic was dead, and Rome was ruled by an emperor. It is possible—even probable—that the Trump figures quoting Pompey do not know this history. But understanding it is not necessary to grasp why Pompey’s words are nothing to emulate, nor to predict what will happen to a republic that allows such leaders to reach and maintain power. Related: No, really, are we Rome? The rise of the fusion Democrat Alexandra Petri: Pajamas would like an apology, Secretary Duffy . Today’s News The Trump administration announced a new rule restricting Chinese companies’ access to advanced American AI chips through overseas data centers, closing a loophole in U.S. export controls. The rule, which takes effect in 90 days, comes amid tensions within the administration over chip restrictions ahead of President Trump’s planned meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping. Trump defended his two-day silence on Friday’s nationwide air-traffic shutdown , saying that he had managed the crisis from the White House while leaving public updates to Cabinet officials. Lindsay Clancy, the Massachusetts mother charged with killing her three young children in 2023, is scheduled to face a second trial beginning March 29, 2027 , after her first trial ended with a hung jury. Prosecutors are expected to pursue first-degree-murder charges again, while Clancy’s defense argues that she was suffering from postpartum psychosis and should not be held criminally responsible. Dispatches Work in Progress : Anthropic’s pitch to investors depends on pursuing the very strategy that it warns could lead to human extinction , Rogé Karma argues. The Wonder Reader : Fully engaging your brain with no distractions can be a reminder of what the mind is capable of , Isabel Fattal writes. Explore all of our newsletters here. Evening Read Tim Warner / Getty Awesome By Adrienne LaFrance In Jules Verne’s wildest imagination, the technology that would send humanity starward was already familiar on Earth. The launching mechanism for the American rocket, in Verne’s 1865 novel From the Earth to the Moon , is—of all things—a colossal cannon. The speed required to reach the lunar surface, he reasoned, would require a gunshot of a launch. So in Vernian terms, a starship was not merely launched but “fired” into space. I’ve been thinking of Verne today as I watched the video (then watched it again, and again) of SpaceX’s latest history-making maneuver. Yesterday, for the first time ever, engineers successfully pulled off a midair landing —using the company’s Mechazilla tower’s “chopstick” arms to snatch a starship the size of a skyscraper out of the sky after it had spent the past 22 hours in Earth’s orbit. Up until this point, Mechazilla’s chopsticks had caught boosters after launch—that is, the part of the rocket that detaches—but never ships themselves. Read the full article. items.title: Burkina Faso : 64 349 compatriotes rapatriés de Guinée, selon le CONASUR
items.description: Retour des Burkinabè affectés par les événements en Guinée : les opérations se poursuivent avec 4 625 personnes accueillies le 15 novembre 2026. Les opérations de rapatriement des ressortissants burkinabè affectés par les événements survenus en Guinée se poursuivent. À la date du dimanche 15 novembre 2026, le Conseil national de secours d’urgence et de réhabilitation (CONASUR) dénombre 64 349 personnes rapatriées depuis le début de l’opération, selon un communiqué du ministère de la Famille et de la Solidarité. Le retour des compatriotes burkinabè se poursuit dans de bonnes conditions. Dans son communiqué daté du 15 novembre 2026, le ministère de la Famille et de la Solidarité indique que les mouvements de retour ont permis d’accueillir, d’enregistrer et de prendre en charge 4 625 personnes au cours de cette seule journée. Ce nouveau bilan porte à 64 349 le nombre total de personnes rapatriées depuis le lancement des opérations. Parmi elles, le CONASUR recense 63 075 hommes et 1 274 femmes. Le communiqué fait également état de 13 527 enfants et de 1 762 ressortissants d’autres nationalités. Plus de 10 000 personnes convoyées vers leurs localités d’origine Au-delà de l’accueil et de la prise en charge des personnes rapatriées, les autorités poursuivent les efforts pour faciliter leur retour dans leurs localités respectives. Grâce à la mobilisation citoyenne dans les différentes régions administratives, les Conseils régionaux de secours d’urgence et de réhabilitation (CORESUR) ont assuré le transport de 10 990 personnes depuis Bobo-Dioulasso vers leurs localités d’origine. Cette assistance vient s’ajouter aux initiatives individuelles de retour. Le CONASUR a, par ailleurs, salué l’engagement des différents acteurs qui contribuent au bon déroulement de cette opération. Il a exprimé sa reconnaissance à l’ensemble des partenaires et des personnes mobilisées pour leur appui, jugé déterminant dans la réussite du dispositif. Le CONASUR appelle à la responsabilité dans le partage des informations Tout en réaffirmant sa volonté de poursuivre le rapatriement des compatriotes encore concernés, le Conseil national invite les populations à maintenir leur élan de solidarité. Il appelle également à davantage de responsabilité dans le partage des informations relatives à cette opération, en privilégiant les sources et les canaux officiels afin d'éviter la propagation d'informations non vérifiées. À travers cette mobilisation, les autorités burkinabè entendent poursuivre l'accompagnement des ressortissants concernés et faciliter leur réinstallation dans leurs localités d'origine. L’article Burkina Faso : 64 349 compatriotes rapatriés de Guinée, selon le CONASUR est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Circle railway fire: One person burnt to death, several shops destroyed
items.description: A man has been burnt to death after a fire swept through the Railways Area behind the State Transport Corporation (STC) station at Kwame Nkrumah Circle in Accra. The extent of the damage and the circumstances surrounding the victim’s death were yet to be fully established as firefighting operations continued for hours. Several wooden structures were engulfed in the Monday night blaze, sending thick smoke billowing into the sky and prompting an emergency response from the Ghana National Fire Service (GNFS). The fire broke out close to the parking areas of VIP and OA Transport Services, near the Kwame Nkrumah Interchange. A member of the GNFS Communications Team, Assistant Divisional Officer I Alex King Nartey, confirmed the death of an adult male, whose identity had not been established at the time of reporting. He told Joy News journalist Collins Frimpong that multiple fire appliances had been dispatched to the scene, with firefighters working to contain the blaze and stop it from spreading to nearby structures. Although the cause of the fire remains unknown, Mr Nartey criticised some squatters at the scene for continuing to smoke despite the raging inferno.

items.title: Gombe approves N97bn road projects, N3.8bn emergency vehicles
items.description: …SEC endorses 2027–2029 expenditure framework, updates social protection policy .. Government targets December resumption of Kolmani oil exploration By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe GOMBE — The Gombe State Executive Council (SEC), presided over by Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, has approved seven road projects valued at billions of naira, covering approximately 97 kilometres across four local government areas of the state. The council also approved the procurement of 40 emergency response and public utility vehicles, comprising 20 firefighting trucks and 20 water tankers, at a combined cost of about N3.8 billion. Other major decisions taken at the council meeting on Monday included the approval of the 2027–2029 Medium-Term Expenditure Framework (MTEF), an updated Social Protection Policy for 2027–2030 and measures to position the state to benefit from the anticipated resumption of oil exploration in the Kolmani area in December. Briefing journalists after the meeting, the Commissioner for Information and Culture, Moses Kyari Bolda, said the decisions reflected the administration’s commitment to infrastructure development, improved public services and long-term economic growth. On the road projects, the Commissioner for Works and Infrastructure, Shehu Yarima Abdullahi, said the council approved seven memoranda presented by his ministry for projects covering Yamaltu-Deba, Balanga, Shongom and Kaltungo Local Government Areas. Among the approved projects is the 18.9-kilometre Talasse-Bangu-Boka Bundi-Walalunguda Road, including a spur to Dalawaja, awarded to Datum Construction Company Limited at N23.98 billion, with a completion period of 24 months. Similarly, the 38-kilometre Lapan-Labariya-Lasanjan-Latatar-Lakunturum Road, with a spur to Burak, was awarded to EEC International Limited at N49.3 billion, also with a 24-month completion period. The council also approved the first phase of the Bangunji-Dadiya-Yelwa-Gombe/Yola Road project, covering approximately 15 kilometres, to be executed by EEC International Limited at N26.3 billion. Other projects include the initial four-kilometre section of the Degri-Sikam-Nyuwar Kindiyo Road, covering Degri to Sikam, awarded to Datum Construction Company Limited at approximately N4 billion. The 10.5-kilometre Dogon Ruwa-Kaltin Road was also awarded to the company at about N10.1 billion, while the nine-kilometre Kurjale-Pata Road was awarded to EEC International Limited. The seventh project, covering 1.5 kilometres of the Kunuwal Road Network, was awarded to Swas Grade Limited. Abdullahi explained that the Degri-Sikam-Nyuwar Kindiyo Road would be implemented in phases, with the initial four-kilometre stretch from Degri to Sikam approved as the first phase. He described the approvals as an expansion of the state’s infrastructure development programme, particularly the administration’s Network 1,100 Kilometres Road Initiative, designed to open up rural communities, improve access to markets and facilitate the movement of people, goods and services. He added that the projects would strengthen inter-community connectivity, promote agricultural and commercial activities and improve access to essential public services. Governor Yahaya, he said, was expected to perform the foundation-laying ceremony for the Talasse-Bangu-Boka Bundi-Walalunguda Road, including the Dalawaja spur, to formally signal the commencement of construction. N3.8bn for emergency vehicles In another development, the council approved the procurement of 20 firefighting trucks and 20 water tankers at a combined cost of approximately N3.8 billion. The Commissioner for Finance, Muhammad Gambo Magaji, said the acquisition of the firefighting trucks would strengthen the operational capacity of the State Fire Service, particularly as the government expands fire service stations beyond the state capital. He explained that the additional water tankers would provide temporary relief to residents while the ongoing revitalisation of the Gombe Regional Water Supply Scheme was being completed, including plans to transition its operations to solar-powered energy. Magaji disclosed that all 40 vehicles would be converted from diesel-powered engines to Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) to reduce fuel expenditure, improve operational efficiency and promote cleaner energy. Kolmani oil exploration Meanwhile, the state government said it had intensified preparations to position Gombe for the anticipated resumption of oil exploration activities in the Kolmani area, with drilling expected to resume in the first week of December 2026. The Commissioner for Energy and Mineral Resources, Sanusi Ahmad Pindiga, said the government was working with Rift Oil Nigeria Limited, a consultant engaged to facilitate the state’s institutional engagement, recognition and registration as an oil and gas-producing state. He disclosed that the consultant had completed 12 of its 14 planned deliverables, representing significant progress in developing the institutional framework and human capital required for the state’s participation in the oil and gas industry. One of the major achievements, according to him, was the training of 100 graduates in artisan skills, including plumbing, carpentry, information and communication technology and welding. The beneficiaries were also provided with starter kits and financial support to enable them establish businesses, become self-reliant and position themselves for employment and entrepreneurial opportunities arising from the anticipated expansion of oil and gas activities. Pindiga said the consultant’s engagements had also facilitated the preparation of relevant documentation and institutional support mechanisms considered necessary for the state’s participation in the emerging petroleum industry. He described the expected resumption of drilling in Kolmani as a significant economic opportunity, stressing the need to prepare the state’s institutions, workforce and communities to benefit from the development. SEC approves 2027–2029 fiscal framework In another major decision, the council approved the Gombe State Medium-Term Expenditure Framework for 2027–2029, which will provide the fiscal and economic projections guiding revenue generation and expenditure priorities over the next three years. The Commissioner for Budget, Micah Sunday Hamman, said the framework would serve as the foundation for preparing the 2027 budget while strengthening fiscal discipline, resource allocation and effective implementation of government programmes. He explained that the MTEF would provide a realistic basis for projecting revenue and expenditure, ensuring that government policies, projects and programmes were aligned with available resources and clearly defined development priorities. The council also approved an updated Gombe State Social Protection Policy for 2027–2030 to strengthen the state’s social welfare system and provide coordinated and sustainable support for vulnerable and disadvantaged citizens. According to Hamman, the policy would consolidate existing government interventions and establish a comprehensive framework for protecting vulnerable groups, particularly children and other citizens requiring social assistance. He identified the five pillars of the policy as social assistance, social insurance, labour market interventions, systems strengthening, and protection against discrimination, violence, exploitation and social exclusion. The commissioner said the framework would emphasise transparency, inclusion and evidence-based implementation to ensure that social protection interventions reached their intended beneficiaries and improved their living conditions. The latest decisions, he added, underscored the state government’s determination to combine infrastructure expansion with sound fiscal management, improved emergency services, social welfare and strategic economic planning as Gombe prepares for its next phase of development. items.title: Mimiko congratulates Aiyedatiwa on Silverbird award
items.description: …Urges Ondo governor to deepen dividends of democracy By Dayo Johnson, Akure Former Governor of Ondo State, Dr Olusegun Mimiko, has congratulated Governor Lucky Orimisan Aiyedatiwa on emerging as the 2026 Silverbird Governor of the Year. Mimiko described the award as recognition of the achievements recorded so far by the Aiyedatiwa administration and its efforts towards developing the state. The award was presented at the 20th edition of the Silverbird Man of the Year Awards held at Eko Hotels, Lagos. In a congratulatory message, the former governor urged Aiyedatiwa to see the recognition as a call to do more for the people of Ondo State and deepen the dividends of democracy. He said the honour by the Silverbird Group showed that the governor’s efforts were receiving recognition beyond the state. “This honour from the Silverbird Group is an acknowledgement that your efforts are being noticed and should, therefore, spur you to do more for the benefit of the greater majority of our compatriots in our dear state,” Mimiko said. He described Ondo State’s selection for the award among the 36 states as encouraging, noting that it reflected efforts being made across different sectors and communities. “It is encouraging to see Ondo State singled out among the 36 states for this award. It speaks to some work being done across sectors and locations in the state,” he added. Mimiko prayed for greater strength and wisdom for Aiyedatiwa as he continues to steer the affairs of the state. items.title: Our debt restructuring secured $11bn in relief – Amin Adam
items.description: Former Finance Minister Dr Mohammed Amin Adam says Ghana secured $11 billion in relief through debt restructuring. He has rejected claims that the repayment schedule was designed to push the country into another default. Speaking to Evans Mensah in an interview on Monday, he accused Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson of taking credit for the gains while questioning the repayment obligations. “We completed the debt restructuring, which gave Ghana $11 billion in debt relief, $5 billion of which was outrightly cancelled by our external creditors, and another $6 billion in debt service savings.” Dr Amin Adam attributed the reduction in Ghana’s debt-to-GDP ratio to the restructuring undertaken before his government left office. “That is what brought the debt-to-GDP ratio to 45%, and because of that, the minister now has fiscal room.” He argued that the current government benefited from the breathing space those negotiations created. He questioned why the minister would celebrate the results while suggesting the repayment terms had deliberately exposed Ghana to default. “And so you are happy to take credit for the benefits, and when it is time for repayment, you are complaining.” Dr Amin Adam described the suggestion that payments were deliberately deferred to 2027 and 2028 to create difficulties for the succeeding government as unfortunate. He said the restructuring was largely complete before the election. He maintained that his government could not have known the National Democratic Congress would be in office when those payments fell due. “98% of the debt restructuring had been completed before we went to election. And so, how on earth could we know that the NDC was going to be in government at the time the repayment will be done in 2027 and 2028?” Responding to the suggestion that an NDC victory was highly probable, he insisted his party fought to retain power. “Yes, but we were determined to break the eight, and we fought the election forcefully, but we lost.” He also said his government had begun servicing some restructured debts before leaving office. He rejected the claim that the repayment structure had set Ghana up for another default.

items.title: The Real Reason Robert Pattinson Is the New James Bond
items.description: Picking a new James Bond has long followed a tried-and-tested formula: Don’t go too famous. The secret agent has nearly always been played by an up-and-coming, well-regarded talent who looks good in a tux. So for years, as the debate has dragged on over who would replace Daniel Craig in the role, dozens of names along those lines have bubbled up; these most recently included Jack Lowden, Callum Turner, and Josh O’Connor. Some possible candidates aged out of the role while waiting for it to open up, in the same way that potential popes find themselves hitting retirement age before their chance at the papacy arrives. But the final choice for the new Bond, Robert Pattinson, completely defies that established logic: By casting someone who’s already globally popular, the franchise is somehow taking the risky version of a typically very safe bet. Pattinson makes plenty of sense on paper as Bond: He’s about the right age (he turned 40 this year) and the right height, at 6 foot 1; he’s debonair and British in all the appreciable ways; he wears a suit better than anyone. (His work in Tenet is one of the best-tailored performances of all time.) But unlike most of his predecessors, he’s also one of the most famous A-listers working today. He’s featured in multiple hit franchises and is also the current occupant of another iconic role, Batman. And because the Bond franchise is in the hands of new ownership for the first time in decades, the old formulas clearly no longer apply. Pattinson’s career started out traditionally enough. He first broke out as a teenager playing Cedric Diggory in the fourth Harry Potter movie before becoming a superstar in his 20s thanks to the Twilight movies—dark romantic fantasies aimed at young adults that were largely dismissed or mocked by critics upon release. But the actor has harnessed his early celebrity to create a constantly shifting and unique persona as a performer. He’s worked with numerous acclaimed directors across genres, Christopher Nolan, David Cronenberg, James Gray, Claire Denis, the Safdie brothers, Robert Eggers, Bong Joon Ho, and Lynne Ramsay among them. When he’s appeared in more conventional blockbusters, he’s put a weird imprimatur on them, as with his emo version of Batman; in December, he’s popping up in Dune: Part Three as an eyebrow-less, shapeshifting villain. [ Read: The James Bond trap ] In a way, playing Bond seems almost too normal for Pattinson. He certainly looks the part in the one promo image that Amazon dropped; he’s a handsome Brit with a chiseled jaw who’s clad in a tux and toting a gun, as per usual for the MI6 super-spy. But one hopes he’ll be able to bring a stranger energy to the role than the Bonds before him. Craig played the character in five movies, culminating in 2021’s No Time to Die ; his take was flinty and frightening, a swerve from Pierce Brosnan’s suave demeanor. Pattinson will likely come across as even more sophisticated—he’s taller and more willowy than Craig, and more traditionally “posh.” And the DC cinematic universe’s recent behind-the-scenes shake-up probably helped Pattinson commit to the franchise, considering that his future as Batman now seems murky. But I hope there’s room in his schedule to maintain the wacky streak he’s shown in movies such as last year’s Mickey 17 , as well as the more alien, lizard-like quality that made his performance in The Batman , along with this year’s The Odyssey and Primetime , so compelling. In previous eras, one would be foolish to hope for that sort of originality. The Bond property had long been a rarity in Hollywood: It was essentially run as a tightly controlled family business. Eon Productions, which was led by the producers Michael G. Wilson and Barbara Broccoli, managed the franchise that they’d inherited from their father; creatively, the buck stopped with them. They relied on a core group of collaborators who knew what a Bond movie should look and feel like, extending beyond whoever was playing the role. That consistency was helpful in building the brand, but it sometimes felt stultifying. Now that Amazon owns Bond outright, the company is making choices that suggest that a more prestigious take on the character is en route. This is not to diss some of the prior Bond films’ directors. Sam Mendes, who made two of the Craig movies, is an Oscar winner—yet he’d made a few flops before he got the gig. Directors such as Cary Fukunaga, Marc Forster, Martin Campbell, and Lee Tamahori were all fairly reliable picks with some large-canvas action experience. But the next installment’s director, Denis Villeneuve, is a glitzy choice: He’s highly regarded by critics and is coming off a giant franchise success of his own with Dune . Among action filmmakers, only Nolan is a bigger name right now (and he was reportedly counted out for the job because he’d require the right to final cut—i.e., total creative control). Amazon’s decision to spare no expense or risk for handling the biggest name-brand property it owns seems obvious. For all the creative ups and downs of the Craig era, the actor was a beloved Bond for 15 years; his memory will be difficult to displace. Rather than roll the dice on a (relative) unknown in search of something new and different, the brand’s new owners are opting for A-list quality. Pattinson is not an outside-the-box choice for Bond. Somehow, he still feels like a total surprise.

items.title: Anambra Patriots endorse APGA-APC alliance, adopt Tinubu for 2027
items.description: By Chimaobi Nwaiwu NNEWI — A political pressure group in Anambra State, Anambra Patriots, APS, has endorsed the alliance between the All Progressives Grand Alliance, APGA, and the All Progressives Congress, APC, adopting President Bola Tinubu as its preferred candidate for the 2027 presidential election. The group also declared its support for the re-election of Anambra State Governor, Professor Chukwuma Soludo, and urged Ndigbo to support his political direction, including his backing for Tinubu. The convener of APS and Anambra State Commissioner for Works, Architect Okey Ezeobi, disclosed the group’s position on Sunday during the Anambra Patriots Women Summit held in Awka, the state capital. Ezeobi expressed dissatisfaction with those criticising Soludo for aligning politically with Tinubu rather than supporting former Anambra State governor and Labour Party presidential candidate in the 2023 election, Peter Obi. He argued that politics should be driven by interests rather than sentiments, insisting that Soludo’s decision to support Tinubu was in the interest of Ndigbo. “My problem with Ndigbo is that they don’t know how to play politics. We do politics of emotion instead of interest. In politics, you get what you contributed, not what you deserve. Politics is about interest,” he said. According to him, Soludo’s support for Tinubu was not motivated by personal gains but by what he described as the need for greater political inclusion of the South-East in national affairs. He said: “Prof. Soludo’s support for Tinubu is not for personal gain, but for the interest of Ndigbo. It is time for Ndigbo to come back to Nigeria. And Soludo is a professor; he has analysed Nigerian politics.” Ezeobi also argued that Soludo should not be criticised for his political choice, saying other ethnic groups had members supporting Obi without attracting similar criticism. He urged Anambra residents to recognise Soludo’s position as governor and support his political decisions, adding that backing Obi was not compulsory for every Igbo politician. “Why is everybody seeing Soludo as an enemy because he is supporting Tinubu? If we accept Soludo as our leader and governor in Anambra State, we must follow him anywhere he is pitching his political tent. It is not compulsory that we must support Peter Obi. Politics is not about sentiments,” he said. The commissioner also made several claims about the political relationship between Obi and Soludo, alleging that Obi had opposed Soludo’s governorship ambition on previous occasions. He cited the 2013, 2021 and 2025 governorship election cycles in Anambra, claiming that Obi had supported different political moves against Soludo, which ultimately failed. Ezeobi, however, maintained that Soludo had not insulted Obi but had only responded to comments he considered critical of Anambra State and APGA. He further criticised the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, describing it as the political platform of a Bayelsa politician, while questioning Obi’s influence within the party. The commissioner said the APS had resolved to support Tinubu in the presidential election while backing APGA candidates in other electoral contests. “Today, we are adopting President Tinubu as the candidate to support in the 2027 presidential election, and we have approved Governor Soludo-led APGA and Tinubu’s APC. We will vote APC in the presidential election and vote APGA in other elections,” he declared. Also speaking, the Secretary to the Anambra State Government, Lady Chiamaka Nnake, a founding member of APS, urged residents to join Soludo in supporting Tinubu. The acting APGA state woman leader and APS woman leader, Mrs Joy Orah, said she was mobilising women across the state’s 21 local government areas to support Tinubu and APGA in the elections. Similarly, the Chairman of APS, Ozoh Ejiamatu Damian Enekwechi, urged the people of the state to follow Soludo’s political direction. “We are only following our leader. That is what we are doing. We must follow our leader in the 2027 presidential election and other elections,” he said. Meanwhile, Vanguard observed that strategic locations across Awka had been adorned with giant campaign billboards bearing the inscription: “Solu Tinubu — The Progressives Train is on Track: Join Now and in Our Own Interest.” The post Anambra Patriots endorse APGA-APC alliance, adopt Tinubu for 2027 appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: True fulfilment lies in impacting lives, says Ooni
items.description: … Backs YASA Foundation’s drive for inclusive society By Ogochukwu Agha lagos—The Ooni of Ife, Oba Adeyeye Ogunwusi, has urged Nigerians, corporate organisations and philanthropists to support initiatives that empower vulnerable people, saying true fulfilment lies in making positive impact on others. The monarch spoke at the unveiling of the Yeye Afolashade Shona-Aluko (YASA) Foundation in Lagos, where he donated N5 million. Describing the foundation’s humanitarian mission as worthy of support, Oba Ogunwusi said: “What gives the greatest happiness in this world is a life of impact and fulfilment. Everybody is chasing money. But when you attain a certain level of wealth, you discover that money does not necessarily bring happiness. “The essence of life is what you can give to others.” Senator Sylvia Mthethwa of Eswatini urged governments and institutions to promote inclusive development, asking: “Are we developing societies in which everybody has an opportunity to participate or contribute and prosper?” She called for improved access to education, healthcare and employment for persons with disabilities. The Ooni’s wife, Olori Temitope Enitan-Ogunwusi, commended the foundation’s founder, urging her to remain committed to humanitarian service despite challenges. Earlier, Shona-Aluko said her youngest son’s disability inspired her intervention. She recalled employing eight specialised teachers to support him and other children at Ikeja High School for about nine years. She said the experience exposed the difficulties faced by families unable to afford specialised education. “YASA Foundation was born from a burden… a burden to give voice to the voiceless, strength to the weak, and to say boldly: ‘You are not forgotten,’” she said. The foundation focuses on inclusive education, healthcare, rehabilitation, assistive devices, vocational training and livelihood support. The event featured beneficiaries’ testimonies and recognition of Shona-Aluko by two international institutions.
