items.title: Expert pushes unified emergency response system to save lives
items.description: By Sola Ogundipe Nigeria needs a unified emergency response system that connects patients to ambulances, appropriately equipped hospitals, medical specialists and health insurance providers through a single call, an emergency care expert and healthcare entrepreneur has stated. Giving the warning in Lagos,during the inaugural ResQ Summit 2026, Dr. Aisha Onisarotu Atanda, who is the Chief Executive Officer of The Ambulance Company, ResQCore and TAC Care, said that the absence of such coordination continues to expose patients to avoidable delays and risks. Atanda, who convened the Summit themed “Building a Coordinated Emergency System”, said an integrated emergency care network would eliminate the burden on patients and their relatives to independently arrange transportation, identify suitable hospitals, secure specialist intervention and negotiate access to treatment during life-threatening situations. Speaking at the Rescue Summit 2026, themed “Building a Coordinated Emergency Care System”, Atanda said Nigeria already had organisations and resources providing different aspects of emergency care, but poor coordination prevented them from functioning as one effective system. She said the current arrangement often left families struggling to determine which emergency number to call, secure an ambulance and identify a hospital capable of managing the patient’s condition, resulting in delays that could compromise survival. “The problem we have at the moment is that many organisations operate in silos. Hospitals operate independently. Ambulance companies and health maintenance organisations are also doing their own thing, all with the right intention of improving emergency care. “However, when these organisations operate in silos, patients and their relatives are left to navigate the system themselves. They have to figure out which number to call, contact an ambulance and then decide where the patient should be taken,” Atanda said. She noted that the proposed model would ensure that once an emergency call was received, the patient’s location and condition would be established, an appropriate ambulance dispatched and a receiving hospital with the capacity to provide the required treatment identified. Atanda said the initiative is particularly important in emergencies involving burns, complicated pregnancies and other conditions requiring specialised intervention, where taking a patient to the wrong facility could result in dangerous delays. “The patient’s relatives may not have the expertise to know, for instance, that a burn victim needs to be taken to a specialist burns centre. As a result, valuable time is wasted accessing the wrong care when the patient could have been connected to the right facility through a coordinated system,” she added. Atanda, who co-founded an ambulance service provider and subsequently developed technology for coordinating emergency services, said her organisation had also extended its activities to intensive care and surgical services through TAC Care at the Lagos State University Teaching Hospital, LASUTH. She said the objective was to demonstrate how an integrated emergency response model could work and encourage governments to adopt and strengthen similar arrangements. On complaints about unanswered emergency calls and delayed ambulance response, Atanda said a properly coordinated system must guarantee round-the-clock communication and effective dispatch of emergency services. “We operate a 24-hour communication centre where someone is available to receive calls, establish the caller’s location and coordinate assistance. The goal is to ensure that patients receive the support they need throughout their emergency care journey,” she said. She added that private sector initiatives could demonstrate workable models that government agencies could subsequently integrate into the national emergency response framework. On the cost of emergency treatment, Atanda acknowledged that quality healthcare remained expensive but argued that health insurance offered one of the most sustainable ways of reducing the financial burden on patients and their families. “We cannot continue to rely on out-of-pocket payments for every healthcare emergency. It is simply not sustainable,” she said. Beyond insurance, Atanda called for stronger government-private sector partnerships, noting that the government had the authority to formulate policies and wider community reach, while private organisations could contribute operational expertise and service delivery capacity. “There should be policies that make health insurance compulsory, while the government can also pool resources and allocate funds specifically for emergency care, “The faster a patient accesses appropriate care, the better the chances of survival and recovery. If it takes days before someone receives treatment, the likelihood of a positive outcome becomes significantly lower,” she said. The emergency care advocate also called for stronger public preparedness, saying Nigerians needed to understand how to recognise emergencies, seek assistance and provide basic first aid before professional responders arrived. She said public education and first aid training were essential because emergency responders might not reach victims immediately after an incident. “When you call for help, it may take at least five minutes for emergency responders to reach you. What do you do during those minutes before help arrives?” she asked. She urged Nigerians to acquire basic skills to recognise conditions such as seizures and strokes, understand the appropriate response and provide accurate information when contacting emergency services. Atanda said her ambulance company provided first aid training for individuals, corporate organisations and healthcare professionals, but stressed the need to expand such programmes and make emergency preparedness part of everyday life. “We need to make emergency response information part of our everyday lives so that people understand how to seek help when emergencies occur,” she said. She maintained that building a functional emergency care system would require sustained collaboration, public education, accessible health insurance and a reliable network capable of connecting patients to appropriate care without unnecessary delays The post Expert pushes unified emergency response system to save lives appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 67th NCH: Nasarawa seeks actionable resolutions to improve healthcare delivery
items.description: By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja The Nasarawa State Government has called on health sector leaders across the country to translate commitments and policy decisions into measurable outcomes that will improve healthcare delivery, particularly at the grassroots. The Governor of the State, Abdullahi Sule, made the call on Monday while declaring open the Technical Session of the 67th National Council on Health (NCH) in Lafia, the state capital. This was contained in a statement signed by the Assistant Director of Information and Public Relations, Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, Ado Bako. Represented by the Deputy Governor, Dr. Emmanuel Akabe, Sule said the Council provided an important platform for stakeholders to develop practical solutions to the challenges confronting Nigeria’s health sector. He expressed confidence that deliberations under the theme, “From Commitments to Results: Delivering Quality and Equitable Healthcare for All Nigerians,” would produce actionable recommendations to strengthen the country’s healthcare system. The Governor described Nasarawa’s selection as host of the national meeting as a privilege and an opportunity to showcase the state’s peaceful environment, hospitality and economic potential. He also reaffirmed the state government’s commitment to supporting national health sector reforms and ensuring a successful meeting. He urged delegates to take advantage of the state’s hospitality during their stay. Earlier, the Nasarawa state Commissioner for Health, Dr. Gwamna Gaza, described the meeting as a historic opportunity for the state to host health sector leaders from across the country for the first time. He stressed that decisions reached at the Council would have far-reaching implications for the country’s health sector, urging participants to remain conscious of the fact that they were also beneficiaries of the policies and reforms being formulated for Nigerians. He also called for active participation and constructive contributions, assuring delegates that the state government and relevant institutions were available to address any challenges they might encounter during the meeting. Presenting the procedures for the Technical Session, the Permanent Secretary of the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare and Chairman of the Technical Committee, Daju Kachollom, said the two-day meeting, scheduled for November 16 and 17, would provide the technical foundation for the main Council meeting on November 19 and 20. She explained that the main Council meeting would be chaired by the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate. According to her, the Technical Committee would review proceedings and the implementation status of resolutions reached at the 66th Regular National Council on Health, consider memoranda submitted by the Federal Government, state governments and other ministries, and develop recommendations for consideration by the Council. Kachollom, said the memoranda submitted for consideration were organised around the four pillars of the Health Sector Strategic Blueprint. The pillars, she listed, were effective governance; efficient, equitable and quality health systems; unlocking value chains; and health security. She said the submissions would address critical areas, including the implementation of the National Health Act, multisectoral health interventions, clinical research and development, as well as strengthening Nigeria’s capacity to detect, prevent and respond to public health threats. These threats, she noted, included cholera, Lassa fever, cerebrospinal meningitis and measles. To ensure focused deliberations, the Permanent Secretary said summaries of the memoranda had been prepared as working documents, while authors would be given five minutes each to present their submissions, highlight key issues and outline recommendations. “The Secretariat will subsequently consolidate the Technical Committee’s recommendations for consideration by the Council,” she said. She also disclosed that the Ministry had adopted an electronic documentation system for the Council, with relevant meeting documents preloaded onto tablets provided to participants. items.title: Diabetes: 3 in 4 Africans unaware as Afonchies screens Lagos residents
items.description: By Chioma Obinna Millions of people living with diabetes in Nigeria and Africa at large risk developing serious health complications because they are unaware of their condition, the International Diabetes Federation (IDF) has warned, underscoring the need for wider access to screening and early diagnosis. The IDF disclosed that approximately 24.6 million adults aged 20–79 were living with diabetes in Africa in 2024, with nearly three out of every four unaware of their condition. The figure highlights the growing public health challenge posed by undiagnosed diabetes and the need for community-based interventions to encourage regular health checks, particularly among people who may not have access to routine medical services. Against this backdrop, Afonchies Pharmacy Limited last Saturday provided free blood glucose and blood pressure screening for residents of Addo, Badore, Langbasa and neighbouring communities in the Ajah area of Lagos State as part of activities marking the 2026 World Diabetes Day. The exercise, held on Saturday, November 14, at the company’s Addo branch, targeted 200 adults and aligned with this year’s theme, “Early Action on Diabetes,” which emphasises early diagnosis and timely intervention to prevent complications. Participants also received health counselling and professional medication advice as part of efforts to improve awareness of diabetes, hypertension and the importance of monitoring key health indicators. Speaking, the Managing Director of Afonchies, Pharm. Adebayo Afon, said the initiative reflected the company’s commitment to making healthcare more accessible and encouraging people to take greater responsibility for their health through regular screening and early intervention. He explained that the company’s community pharmacy model went beyond dispensing medicines to providing health education, identifying potential health risks and connecting people to appropriate care. Afon also emphasised the importance of community-based interventions in addressing the burden of undiagnosed diabetes and hypertension. Speaking on the activities at the screening centre, the Chief Pharmacist representing the Addo branch, Pharm. Michael Akpala, said the exercise was designed to address the fear and cost that often discourage people from checking their blood sugar and blood pressure. He disclosed that beneficiaries with concerning results would receive counselling and be linked to nearby primary healthcare facilities, including those in Addo and Badore, for further evaluation and care. He added that the company hoped to build on the initiative by encouraging regular health checks. Also speaking, the Chief Operating Officer, Pharm. Oluwatosin Majoyeogbe, disclosed that Afonchies currently had 13 active branches, with another nearing completion. He said the company intended to make the screening programme an annual event, rotating it across different communities where it operates. Majoyeogbe also highlighted the company’s online ordering platform, which allows customers to submit prescriptions, select their preferred branch, arrange medicine delivery or collect their orders, subject to regulatory requirements. Community pharmacies, he said, serve as the first point of healthcare contact for many residents, making them important in promoting medication safety and appropriate treatment. One of the beneficiaries, 78-year-old elder statesman, Mr Samuel Akinrinifin, commended Afonchies for the initiative, describing it as a valuable opportunity, particularly for elderly residents, to monitor their health. Akinrinifin, who said regular health checks had been part of his personal healthcare routine, expressed satisfaction with the exercise, adding that he had never been hospitalised because of his commitment to regular monitoring. He urged Afonchies and other healthcare providers to sustain such initiatives and extend them to more elderly people. World Diabetes Day is observed annually on November 14 to raise awareness about diabetes and promote prevention, early diagnosis and effective management. The high proportion of people living with diabetes without knowing their status highlights the importance of accessible screening, public education and timely referral to health facilities to reduce the risk of complications. items.title: Nollywood stars, iconic comedians rally support for Hajiya Hadiza Foundation
items.description: By Chioma Obinna Leading Nigerian Nollywood actors and celebrated comedians have pledged their support for the Hajiya Hadiza Foundation (HHF), commending its President and Founder, Ambassador Hadiza Umar, for her humanitarian interventions among vulnerable Nigerians. The entertainers made their commitment at a press conference held in Abuja over the weekend, where they applauded the Foundation’s efforts in supporting widows of fallen heroes, victims of terrorism, internally displaced persons (IDPs), indigent students and other less privileged members of society. Over the years, the Foundation has implemented various humanitarian and empowerment programmes, including economic support for widows, educational scholarships for disadvantaged students and interventions in communities affected by insecurity and poverty. Speaking at the event, veteran Nollywood actor, Chief Jide Kosoko, described Ambassador Umar’s humanitarian activities as a reflection of her personal experiences and understanding of the challenges faced by disadvantaged people. Kosoko noted that Umar’s difficult childhood, during which she lost both parents and 12 siblings at the age of 13, had shaped her determination to support people experiencing poverty, deprivation and hardship. He urged well-to-do Nigerians to emulate her philanthropic disposition and contribute to efforts aimed at improving the living conditions of vulnerable citizens. “We must all rally round to support the humanitarian works of this young lady. There are many Nigerians who are far richer than her but have refused to help the less privileged. I urge wealthy individuals to emulate the kind gesture of the Hajiya Hadiza Foundation. We promise to support you through our various platforms,” he said. Also speaking, popular comedian Julius Agwu commended the Foundation for its interventions among vulnerable women, widows, orphans, poor students and other disadvantaged groups. Agwu disclosed that his foundation would explore collaboration with HHF, particularly in economic empowerment initiatives targeting women and young people in rural communities. In his remarks, veteran Nollywood actor and octogenarian, Chief Chika Okpala, popularly known as Zebrudaya, appealed to the Foundation to extend its humanitarian interventions to struggling veterans in the entertainment industry. He called attention to the plight of some veteran Nollywood actors, musicians and comedians facing financial difficulties, poverty and health challenges, urging the Foundation to consider providing them with assistance. Okpala also praised Ambassador Umar’s commitment to economic empowerment programmes in underserved communities and internally displaced persons’ camps. Responding, an emotional Ambassador Umar disclosed that the Foundation had implemented humanitarian and economic empowerment programmes worth approximately N850 million nationwide over the past three years, with particular attention to IDP camps and underserved communities. She explained that the interventions included skills acquisition training, livelihood support, scholarship awards and the distribution of thousands of grinding machines, sewing machines, hairdressing and barbing kits, generators and cash assistance to beneficiaries. According to her, the programmes are designed to promote self-reliance, restore dignity and provide sustainable livelihood opportunities for vulnerable individuals and families. Ambassador Umar described the Foundation as a lasting legacy she hopes to bequeath to her child, expressing appreciation to the entertainment industry veterans for identifying with its humanitarian mission. She said their support would further strengthen the Foundation’s capacity to sustain and expand its interventions across the country. The event underscored the growing involvement of members of Nigeria’s creative industry in humanitarian advocacy and efforts to mobilise support for vulnerable populations. items.title: Du micro de la RTB à l’engagement politique : Do Pascal Sessouma s’est éteint à l’âge de 69 ans à Montréal
items.description: Le monde des médias et de la politique burkinabè pleure l'une de ses figures emblématiques. Do Pascal Kiemdoro Sessouma, connu sous le pseudonyme de « DPS », s'est éteint à l'âge de 69 ans dans la nuit du samedi 14 au dimanche 15 novembre 2026 à Montréal, au Canada. L'annonce de sa disparition a été faite ce lundi 16 novembre par la Radiodiffusion Télévision du Burkina (RTB) lors de son journal télévisé de 13 heures. Tour à tour grand reporter, rédacteur en chef à la RTB, grand reporter à Télé-Québec, enseignant à l'ISTIC et candidat à l'élection présidentielle de 2020, cet homme aux multiples casquettes laisse derrière lui un parcours marquant. Le monde de la presse burkinabè vient de perdre l'un de ses acteurs majeurs. Do Pascal Kiemdoro Sessouma, affectueusement surnommé « DPS », a définitivement déposé sa plume à l'âge de 69 ans à Montréal. Né en 1957 à N’Dorla, il s'est imposé au fil des décennies comme un professionnel accompli de l'information au Burkina Faso. C'est au sein de la Radiodiffusion Télévision du Burkina (RTB) qu'il a bâti une part essentielle de sa carrière, s'illustrant en tant que grand reporter avant d'occuper les responsabilités de rédacteur en chef. À travers ces fonctions, il a activement contribué à la production et à l'encadrement de l'information publique. La trajectoire professionnelle de Do Pascal Sessouma s'est également poursuivie au-delà des frontières nationales. Au cours de sa carrière, son expérience l'a notamment conduit au Canada, où il a exercé comme grand reporter pour la chaîne Télé-Québec. Soucieux de partager son savoir-faire avec les jeunes générations, il s'est également investi dans l'enseignement à l'Institut des sciences et techniques de l'information et de la communication (ISTIC), participant ainsi à la formation de nombreux jeunes professionnels des médias. Au-delà des métiers de l'information et de la transmission, Do Pascal Sessouma a pris une part active dans la vie politique nationale. En 2020, il a franchi un cap décisif en fondant le parti politique « Vision Burkina ». Sous cette bannière, il a participé à l'élection présidentielle organisée la même année, marquant ainsi son entrée dans la compétition politique au Burkina Faso. Avec sa disparition, le pays perd un homme polyvalent dont l'itinéraire aura traversé avec conviction le journalisme, la formation et la politique. L’article Du micro de la RTB à l'engagement politique : Do Pascal Sessouma s'est éteint à l'âge de 69 ans à Montréal est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: We did not defer debt payments to make NDC default – Amin Adam
items.description: Former Finance Minister Dr Mohammed Amin Adam has rejected claims that the previous government deliberately deferred debt repayments to 2027 and 2028 to make the NDC government default. Speaking to Evans Mensah on Monday, he described Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson’s assessment of the repayment arrangements as wrong. “What struck me, as far as that [DDEP] is concerned, was the minister standing in Parliament and saying that we deliberately deferred the payment to 2027-2028 in order for them to default; that was very, very unfortunate for me to hear from the minister.” Dr Amin Adam said 98% of the debt restructuring had been completed before the election. He questioned how the previous administration could have designed the repayment schedule around an NDC victory. “And so, how on earth could we know that the NDC was going to be in government at the time the repayment will be done in 2027 and 2028?” When asked whether the likelihood of a change in government influenced the arrangements, he insisted the NPP expected to retain power. “Yes, but we were determined to break the eight, and we fought the election forcefully, but we lost.” He said the government had campaigned to win and continue servicing the debt. It had also begun paying some bondholders before leaving office. Dr Amin Adam accused the Finance Minister of taking credit for the gains from restructuring while criticising the repayment obligations. According to him, the exercise secured $11 billion in debt relief. This included $5 billion in outright cancellation by external creditors and $6 billion in debt-service savings. He argued that these gains reduced Ghana’s debt-to-GDP ratio and created fiscal room for the current government. “And so you are happy to take credit for the benefits, and when it is time for repayment, you are complaining.” His central objection was that the repayment timetable was being presented as a deliberate political trap, despite the benefits the current government had received from the same restructuring.

items.title: Drug insecurity threatens national security, pharmacists warn FG
items.description: … Seeks 1% of seized drug trafficking assets to fund enforcement … Demands government control of medicine supply chain By Chioma Obinna The Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria (PSN) on Monday warned that pharmaceutical insecurity poses a serious threat to Nigeria’s national security, urging the Federal Government to strengthen regulatory control of medicines and prevent the transfer of critical drug management responsibilities from public authorities to private interests. The society also called for the establishment of a special fund to tackle illicit financial flows in the healthcare sector, proposing that one per cent of assets seized from drug trafficking be dedicated to strengthening the enforcement activities of the Pharmacy Council of Nigeria (PCN) and the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC). The resolutions were contained in a communiqué issued at the end of the 99th Annual National Conference of the PSN, tagged IJELE 2026, held from November 2 to 7 at the International Convention Centre, Awka, Anambra State. The conference, which brought together pharmacists and other stakeholders in the pharmaceutical and healthcare sectors, was held under the theme, “One Health, One Pharmacy: Bridging Knowledge, Practice and Policy for National Impact.” In the communiqué signed by the President, Pharm. Ibrahim Tanko Ayuba, and National Secretary, Pharm. Gafar Madehin, the pharmacists maintained that medicines were not merely commercial commodities but matters of permanent regulatory control and national security. Citing Part I, Item 21 of the Second Schedule of the 1999 Constitution, the conference argued that the government’s responsibility for drug regulation and control could not be compromised by private-sector participation in the pharmaceutical supply chain. It cautioned against what it described as a private takeover of drug distribution responsibilities at the public-sector level, warning that such an arrangement could weaken inter-agency collaboration among the PCN, NAFDAC and the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA). The communiqué stated: “Conference reminded Government that drugs are a matter of permanent regulatory control and National Security, which is why it is listed as Part I item 21, in the 2nd Schedule of the 1999 Constitution.” It added that while government could engage private-sector expertise in financing and technology deployment, it should not surrender its regulatory standing or the cooperation currently extended by relevant agencies to Federal Central Medical Stores and Federal Health Institutions. The PSN further called for the integration of community pharmacies into Nigeria’s national security architecture and the Nigeria Health Insurance Authority’s proposed Pharmacy First initiative. According to the conference, more than 10,000 community pharmacies across the country could serve as frontline health and security stakeholders by identifying and reporting suspicious drug-related activities. The pharmacists also urged the Federal Government to support the Drug Revolving Fund and Federal Drug Management Agency Bill, which has passed its first reading at the House of Representatives. They proposed that the agency should serve as a single purchasing and supply platform for medicines, while government pharmacists should retain responsibility for procurement decisions, quality assurance, storage, dispensing and the handling of controlled medicines in the civil service. On the existing Memorandum of Understanding between the Federal Ministry of Health and Medipool, the conference called for a review to limit private-sector participation to pooled price negotiations or competitively selected framework suppliers on a non-exclusive basis, in line with the Procurement Act. To drive the proposed reforms, the PSN recommended a Federal Government-initiated Independent Presidential Committee on the Pharmaceutical Sector, to be chaired by a registered pharmacist recommended by the society, with representation from the PCN, NAFDAC, the National Institute for Pharmaceutical Research and Development and the PSN. The conference called for greater involvement of pharmacists in humanitarian operations, particularly in emergencies and situations involving displacement. It noted that humanitarian crises frequently disrupt access to essential medicines and healthcare services, leaving displaced persons, especially those living with chronic conditions, vulnerable to interruptions in treatment. The conference urged the development of a stronger humanitarian pharmacy workforce equipped to support medicine supply systems, maintain access to essential medicines, assist in chronic disease management and provide pharmaceutical care in emergency settings. It said pharmacists’ expertise in medicine selection, storage, supply, dispensing and appropriate use should be better integrated into national humanitarian preparedness and response plans. On the broader health sector, the pharmacists warned that Nigeria could not achieve meaningful national development while citizens remained frequently ill, essential medicines were inaccessible and health institutions operated in isolation. They identified five strategic bridges needed to transform the country’s health system: implementation, financing, medicine sovereignty, integration and accountability. The conference stressed the need for connected knowledge, coordinated professional practice, coherent policies and accountable leadership, urging government to translate policy commitments into measurable outcomes and lasting health impact. It also applauded the collaboration between the PSN and the West African Society of Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition (WASPEN), calling for a standardised framework to improve workforce planning and integrate advanced pharmacists into multidisciplinary clinical teams. The conference welcomed the harmonisation of the PSN-WASPEN initiative with the Pharmacy Council of Nigeria’s mandatory continuing professional development training modules. On workers’ welfare, the PSN commended the Nigeria Labour Congress, Trade Union Congress and the Joint Health Sector Unions/Assembly of Healthcare Professional Associations for sustaining the struggle for justice and equity in the health sector. It appealed to the labour centres to conclude negotiations on the adjustment of the Consolidated Health Salary Structure (CONHESS), which it said had lingered for about 13 years, while ensuring that JOHESU/AHPA members were not shortchanged in ongoing collective bargaining negotiations. The conference also called for speedy construction of the Pharmacy House at Victoria Island through a developer under a well-structured timeline, while directing the PSN leadership to address outstanding entitlements of debenture subscribers and regularise the documentation of its properties. It further endorsed a one-time support contribution proposed by the PSN President to facilitate the society’s centenary celebrations scheduled for March 2027, challenging the planning committee to deliver what it described as the biggest professional event ever hosted in Nigeria. At the end of the conference, Pharm. Ibrahim Tanko Ayuba emerged as PSN President for the 2026/2027 year. Other members elected into the National Executive Committee include Pharm. Aisha Tukur Isiaku, Deputy President (North); Pharm. (Prof.) Henri A. Okeri, Deputy President (South); Pharm. Ndukwe Uma Ndukwe, National Secretary; and Pharm. Ehitare Patrick Omoarebu, Assistant National Secretary. Also elected were Pharm. Jelili Kilani Adewale, Treasurer; Pharm. Sani Ali Yusuf, Financial Secretary; Pharm. Lizette Njideka Ezenekwe, Publicity Secretary; and Pharm. (Prof.) Sunday A. Adesegun, Editor-in-Chief. The conference expressed appreciation to the Anambra State Government and residents for their hospitality and support throughout the five-day gathering. items.title: Vaccination animale et d’insémination artificielle 2026-2027 : le ministre Amadou Dicko salue la mobilisation dans le Nazinon, Oubri et Yaadga
items.description: Du 10 au 12 novembre 2026, le ministre délégué chargé des ressources animales, Amadou Dicko, a conduit une mission de supervision de la campagne nationale de vaccination et d’insémination artificielle dans les régions du Nazinon, de Oubri et de Yaadga. Le ministère de l’Agriculture, de l’Eau, des Ressources animales et halieutiques entend s’enquérir du dérou-lement de la double campagne de vaccination contre les maladies animales prioritaires et d’insémination artificielle au titre de l’année 2026-2027. A cet effet, le ministre délégué chargé des ressources animales, Amadou Dicko, accompagné du directeur général des services vétérinaires, le vétérinaire-capitaine Aboubacar Nacro, du directeur général du Centre de promotion de l’aviculture et de multiplication des animaux performants, Ardiouma Sirima, ainsi que d’une délégation gouvernementale, a effectué du 10 au 12 novembre 2026, une tournée dans plusieurs localités des régions du Nazinon, de Oubri et du Yaadga. A l’issue de cette tournée de supervision, le ministre Amadou Dicko, a dressé un bilan jugé satisfaisant de l’ensemble des localités visitées. Il a confié que cette opération constitue la quatrième campagne de vaccination d’envergure menée par le gouvernement. Selon lui, l’ambition, à terme, est de maîtriser la plupart des pathologies animales afin de réduire leur impact à l’échelle nationale et d’éradiquer certaines d’entre elles à l’horizon 2030. Le mi-nistre Dicko a indiqué que la dynamique observée sur le terrain est encou-rageante, grâce à l’engagement des autorités locales et à la forte mobilisation des éleveurs. « La vaccination des animaux est obli-gatoire. Nous n’hésiterons pas à sanctionner tout producteur réfractaire », a-t-il martelé. Il a souligné que la majorité des vaccins sont fortement subventionnés, tandis que d’autres sont entièrement gratuits afin de faciliter l’accès aux soins vétérinaires. Sur le plan structurel, le ministre a évoqué les importants investissements en cours dans le domaine de la santé animale, notamment la construction d’une unité nationale de fabrication de vaccins à Samandéni, ainsi que l’opérationnalisation de la centrale d’achat des médicaments vétérinaires et de ses représentations régionales. Il a fermement rappelé le caractère impératif de cette opération. Il a, par ailleurs, annoncé la tenue d’un ate-lier bilan à mi-parcours, le 27 novembre 2026, qui permettra de formuler des recommandations en vue de garantir le succès de la campagne. Il a également insisté sur l’importance de l’insémination artificielle, qu’il considère comme un levier majeur pour amé-liorer le potentiel génétique du cheptel national et accroître durablement les productions de viande et de lait, en cohérence avec l’Offensive agro-pastorale, hydrau-lique et halieutique 2026-2028. Des performances techniques saluées Le vétérinaire capitaine Aboubacar Nacro, (uniforme) a participé activement aux opérations. Dans la région du Nazinon, où la délégation s’est rendue, le directeur général des services vétérinaires, le capitaine Aboubacar Nacro, s’est dit satisfait de l’évolution des opérations à mi-parcours. Il a notamment salué les résultats enregistrés au niveau des petits ruminants, avec environ 300 000 têtes déjà vaccinées contre la Peste des petits ruminants (PPR) et la pasteurellose. Selon lui, ces performances encourageantes témoignent de l’engagement constant des équipes techniques sur le terrain ainsi que de l’adhésion effective des producteurs. Sur le volet de l’amélioration génétique et de la traçabilité, le directeur général du Centre de promotion de l’aviculture et de multiplication des animaux performants, Ardiouma Sirima, a fait savoir que, dans la région de Oubri, un réel engouement des éleveurs est observé depuis le lancement des activités d’insémination artificielle. Près de 650 vaches ont déjà été inséminées dans cette zone. Ardiouma Sirima a également expliqué que l’insémination artificielle est désormais couplée à l’identification numérique des animaux à l’aide de boucles RFID (identification par radio-fréquence). Ce dispositif attribue un identifiant unique à chaque bête, permettant ainsi de lutter efficacement contre le vol de bétail, de retracer son parcours sanitaire jusqu’à l’abattoir et de suivre sa filiation génétique. Le directeur général a tenu à lever toute ambiguïté d’ordre culturel ou religieux concernant l’insémination artificielle. Il a affirmé que des consultations ont été menées auprès des guides religieux et qu’aucune prescription religieuse n’interdit cette pratique moderne, qui contribue au renforcement de la souveraineté alimentaire. Satisfecit des producteursSur les différents sites visités, les bénéficiaires ont exprimé leur reconnaissance aux autorités pour la réduction consi-dérable du coût des vaccins et l’amélioration des rendements de leurs troupeaux. A Toécé dans la région du Nazinon, le Conseiller villageois de développement (CVD), Marou Ilboudo, a salué les effets directs de la campagne sur la survie du bétail. Il a rappelé que, par le passé, malgré les efforts des éleveurs, les épizooties décimaient régulièrement les troupeaux. Marou Ilboudo a souligné que, depuis l’instauration des subventions sur les produits vétérinaires et le déploiement des agents sur le terrain, une baisse considérable de la mortalité animale est constatée, contribuant ainsi à préserver les moyens de subsistance des populations. Toujours dans la région du Nazinon, au village de Sondré-Est, dans la commune de Bindé, l’éleveur Adou Barry a expliqué qu’aupa-ravant, les éleveurs devaient parcourir des dizaines de kilomètres pour faire vacciner leurs animaux. Selon lui, grâce à l’action du gouvernement, le village dispose désormais d’un parc de vaccination, des produits subventionnés et de l’accompa-gnement des agents vétérinaires, garantissant un suivi sanitaire régulier. Des coûts accessibles aux producteurs Dans la région de Oubri, au village de Bangré-Saanga, commune de Mogtédo, province du Ganzourgou, l’éleveur Issa Compaoré a révélé qu’une opération d’insémination artificielle, qui coûtait auparavant 75 000 F CFA, est désormais accessible aux producteurs à seulement 5 000 F CFA grâce à la subvention de l’Etat. Il a souligné la réactivité et la disponibilité permanente des agents vétérinaires aux côtés des éleveurs, ce qui permet d’intervenir rapidement dès qu’un comportement inhabituel est constaté au sein d’un troupeau. Illustrant les retombées économiques et productives de l’insémination artificielle, Issa Compaoré a indiqué qu’avec une seule vache issue de cette technique, il parvient aujourd’hui à obtenir au moins 18 litres de lait par jour. De plus, la valeur marchande des animaux issus de cette technologie connaît une hausse. L’éleveur de Bangré-Saanga a confié qu’un acheteur lui a récemment proposé en vain plus d’un million de F CFA pour acquérir l’un de ses veaux âgés de seulement sept mois. Dans la région de Yaadga, dernière étape de la tournée ministérielle, l’éleveur Boureima Kindo s’est réjoui de la visite des autorités dans sa région. Il a témoigné que, si autrefois les maladies décimaient les troupeaux, la vaccination contribue désormais à protéger le cheptel, à favoriser son accroissement et à garantir une viande de meilleure qualité, essentielle à la santé des consommateurs. Boureima Kindo a souligné l’importance du respect strict des protocoles vétérinaires, avertissant que tout éleveur qui ne s’y conforme pas en subit lui-même les conséquences. Concernant l’insémination artificielle, l’éleveur de Yaadga a expliqué que, lorsque les consignes sont respectées, une vache peut mettre bas chaque année, contre un intervalle de deux à trois ans en cas de reproduction naturelle. Il s’est également félicité de pouvoir accéder, grâce à cette technique, à des races performantes offrant un meilleur rendement en viande. Julien ZOUNGRANA

items.title: Burkina Faso : L’information sanitaire en langues nationales rapproche les soins des populations de Oubri
items.description: Lancée officiellement le 2 novembre dernier par le ministère de la Santé, la campagne du « Mois de la communication sanitaire en langues nationales » bat son plein dans plusieurs régions du pays. Cette initiative, qui vise à rapprocher l’information sanitaire des populations, a conduit les journalistes, ce 16 novembre 2026, à Ziniaré, afin d’échanger avec les acteurs impliqués dans sa mise en œuvre. Dans la région de Oubri, l’information sanitaire prend une dimension de proximité grâce à la mobilisation conjointe des acteurs de santé et des médias locaux. L’ambition du ministère est de faire tomber les barrières linguistiques afin que les messages de prévention et de sensibilisation soient pleinement compris et appropriés par les populations. Pour soulager les ménages face aux dépenses de santé, plusieurs mesures d’allègement ont été instaurées. Sur le plan des infrastructures, la région a vu la construction de 31 formations sanitaires, dont 21 Centres de santé et de promotion sociale (CSPS). À ce jour, 27 de ces structures sont déjà fonctionnelles, tandis que d’autres ouvertures sont attendues dans les mois à venir. L’effort logistique s’est également traduit par l’acquisition de cliniques mobiles et de véhicules de supervision, ainsi que par la mise en service d’un scanner au Centre hospitalier régional (CHR). La communication sanitaire en langues nationales gagne du terrain dans la région de Oubri -©Faso7 Selon le Dr Ambroise Ouédraogo, Directeur général de la santé de Oubri, les efforts de sensibilisation s’appuient sur une collaboration étroite avec les médias de la région. Grâce à l’implication des radios locales de Ziniaré, Boussé et Zorgho, des émissions interactives sont programmées chaque semaine, avec des diffusions synchronisées pour garantir une large couverture. Pour lui, ces espaces d’échange permettent de sensibiliser le public sur des sujets prioritaires tels que la santé communautaire et la lutte contre les décès maternels et néonatals. « Concernant le déroulement du Mois de la communication sanitaire, dès les préparatifs, nous avons pu toucher les différentes radios locales. Il faut souligner que des promoteurs se sont vraiment mis à la tâche pour nous accompagner dans la réalisation des activités de ce mois de communication en santé », a-t-il déclaré. À travers les ondes des radios partenaires, les spécialistes de la santé échangent directement avec les citoyens en mooré. Ces tribunes radiophoniques permettent aux auditeurs de poser leurs questions sans tabou, d’exprimer leurs préoccupations quotidiennes et d’obtenir des réponses fiables et accessibles. Les professionnels de santé engagés Selon Bouraman Sannan, directeur général de la radio Bassy FM, le programme s'articule autour de rencontres directes avec les professionnels de santé engagés dans la vulgarisation médicale. Ces échanges impliquent également les responsables et animateurs des radios partenaires, véritables relais entre le système de santé et les foyers, ainsi que les populations et auditeurs, acteurs principaux de cette dynamique participative. « L'engouement est réel. La santé intéresse beaucoup les gens. Dès qu'il y a une émission sur la santé, ils n'hésitent pas et participent vraiment activement », a-t-il indiqué. Lazard KOLA Faso7 L’article Burkina Faso : L’information sanitaire en langues nationales rapproche les soins des populations de Oubri est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: Three fire tenders deployed as fire hits Tema Community 1 Market
items.description: Firefighters are battling to contain a fire outbreak at the Tema Community 1 Market, near the Community 1 Police Station. Three fire tenders have been dispatched to the scene as personnel of the Ghana National Fire Service (GNFS) work to bring the blaze under control and prevent it from spreading to adjoining shops. The outbreak was reported on Monday, November 16, 2026, with the GNFS confirming the deployment in an update shared on social media platforms. The cause of the fire, the number of shops affected and the extent of damage had not been established at the time of reporting. There were also no immediate reports of casualties. The incident has renewed concerns about fire safety at the busy market, which has experienced previous outbreaks. In February this year, a fire at the same market destroyed two shops and partially damaged four others. No casualties were recorded in that incident, according to the Ghana National Fire Service.

items.title: EU: Countries Plan Rwanda Deportation Centers
items.description: Click to expand Image Left to right: Netherland's Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen, German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt, Austrian Interior Minister Gerhard Karner, Austria's Chancellor Christian Stocker, Rwanda's Interior Minister Vincent Biruta, Greek Minister of Integration Athanasios Plevris, and Denmark's Integration Minister Morten Bodskov, hold a press conference after migration talks in Vienna, Austria, November 16, 2026. © 2026 Heinz-Peter Bader/AP Photo (Brussels) – Negotiations to set up an offshore deportation center in Rwanda, which has a shocking human rights record, is a particularly cruel departure from founding values of the European Union, Human Rights Watch said today. After months of speculation, Austria, Denmark, Germany, Greece, and the Netherlands, alongside Rwanda’s interior minister, confirmed the negotiations on November 16, 2026, on the sidelines of the Vienna Migration Conference organized by the International Centre for Migration Policy Development. The five EU countries confirmed their plan to send people whose asylum claims have been rejected in the EU to Rwanda starting in 2027. “History has shown that third country transfers violate rights and cause suffering,” said Judith Sunderland, senior associate refugee and migrant rights director at Human Rights Watch. “The choice of a country that has an abysmal human rights record and resists international scrutiny tracks with that history and evokes deep skepticism that any nominal rights safeguards will be respected.” The recently enacted EU Return Regulation allows member states to set up deportation centers, “return hubs,” in countries outside the EU where people, including families with children, will be sent if they cannot be deported directly to their country of origin. The regulation states that agreements should be reached only with countries that respect international human rights law. Rwanda does not meet this requirement, Human Rights Watch said, yet the five European countries did not provide any human rights or due diligence assessment during the announcement. The Rwandan government has a well-established record of repressing dissent, including attacks on rights defenders. Its arrests of critics and dissidents, their ill-treatment in detention, and the government’s interference with the judiciary and failure to investigate suspicious deaths have contributed to a widespread climate of fear and self-censorship. In addition, the Rwandan military provides critical support to and exercises overall control over the M23 armed group in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. Both Rwandan forces and the M23 are responsible for serious abuses and war crimes. As recently as January, Germany, Greece, Denmark, and the Netherlands raised concerns about Rwanda at its UN human rights review. A similar UK-Rwanda deal raised serious human rights concerns before it was abandoned, an Israel-Rwanda deal led to documented abuse, and the situation of recent deportees from the United States to Rwanda remains largely unknown. In addition to the threat of harm to those deported to Rwanda, the deal risks financing and giving political leverage to a government responsible for serious human rights abuses at home and abroad, Human Rights Watch said. It could lead the EU to downplay Rwanda’s problematic human rights record or shy away from pressing for measurable improvements. Human Rights Watch has consistently found that deportations to third countries expose people to arbitrary detention, ill-treatment, destitution, and onward returns to harm in their home countries, as well as other serious human rights abuse. The United Nations special rapporteur on the rights of migrants, the Council of Europe commissioner for human rights, and the African Commission on Human and Peoples’ Rights have all cautioned against forcible third-country transfers. The EU countries involved in the deal with Rwanda are bound by the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights and the European Convention on Human Rights. “Forcibly deporting people, including children, to a country where the evidence points to their rights being at risk, is a striking abdication of responsibility and humanity,” Sunderland said. “A deal with Rwanda is likely to cause real harm in addition to not achieving any defensible policy objective.”

items.title: Sorry, Robert Pattinson Is Not James Bond
items.description: Robert Pattinson is, I’m sure, a fine actor. I cannot vouch for this because I have not seen him in movies I’ve liked. Granted, I have not seen his entire body of work; I was already in my 40s when he landed his big role as a vampire in Twilight , a movie that was not exactly aimed at my demographic. I am a fan of superhero movies, and he was, in my view, a terrible Batman: He made Bruce Wayne into a dull cop in a costume. Still, he seems to be working a lot, so someone out there likes him. But is he James Bond? No. Amazon MGM Studios, which now owns the movie franchise, announced today that he’ll take over the role. Yet Pattinson lacks the manly gravitas, the physicality, the wit, to play the world’s most dangerous spy. I’m a Bond superfan. As a kid, I saw the Sean Connery movies only on television. I was 13 when I saw my first Bond film on a big screen: Live and Let Die , starring Roger Moore. It was a revelation. (I was old enough to start getting the jokes about sex, for one thing.) I then devoured, in proper sequence, all the Ian Fleming novels that inspired the movies. When I visited London as a teen in 1975, I didn’t care about seeing Parliament or the crown jewels. I wanted to be Moore—hey, he was the only movie Bond working at the time—and wander the streets once walked by the British spy who always saved the world and got the girl. I know the voice, mannerisms, and quips of every cinematic Bond. I also know what Fleming’s Bond looks and sounds like. According to Fleming, he was based on the 1940s bandleader Hoagy Carmichael, if that makes any sense to you, and I even know where Bond’s boss, M, has his office and his favorite club. (I also know his full name: Miles Messervy. You’re welcome.) I know what Bond’s maid, May, makes him every day for breakfast. In other words, I know James Bond. James Bond is a friend of mine. And Robert Pattinson, you are no James Bond. [ From the March 2024 issue: The James Bond trap ] Bond does not need to be a hairy bruiser; in the movies he loses plenty of fights, and in the books he routinely gets beaten to a pulp and ends up in the enemy’s clutches. Connery was perhaps the most macho of the Bonds, whereas Moore was the most dainty. All of them, however, were charismatic rogues, mature adults who could shoot, fight, drink, and—well, other things. They enjoyed every martini and they made a play for every shapely woman who crossed their path. (Bond is suave and a hero, but he’s also a boozy, sexist boor.) Can Pattinson carry the legacy of any of his predecessors? Aficionados will disagree on who made the best Bond, but each actor had a niche. Connery was a product of the Cold War and the swinging ’60s. (He came back to play Bond once in 1971, Diamonds Are Forever , a misfire that included fitting him with a bad toupee; he made one more mediocre Bond film in 1983 with a different production company as a one-off outside the “canonical” Bond series.) A temporary replacement Bond, an Australian named George Lazenby, did a fine job in one movie, and then blew his career by walking away from the character. Moore, like the rest of us, did his best to make his way through the silly 1970s, but I think he is underappreciated: His 007 grimly faced down Christopher Lee in The Man With the Golden Gun and dispatched not one but two genocidal freaks bent on planetary destruction: a web-fingered weirdo in The Spy Who Loved Me and a eugenics-obsessed, space-industry billionaire—a plot clearly ahead of its time—in Moonraker . Moore was a decent Bond, but stayed with the role too long. In 1985, the 57-year-old Moore had a love scene with 36-year-old Grace Jones in A View to a Kill . Let us not speak of it again. Timothy Dalton, another underappreciated Bond, was an accomplished Shakespearean actor who moved into the role easily, and brought a combination of Connery’s violent physicality and Moore’s caddish humor. (Watch the pre-credits sequence of The Living Daylights , which is one of the best cold opens in the entire series.) Producers had begun looking at the next Bond, Pierce Brosnan, when he was still playing the TV detective Remington Steele and was too young and callow to play a spy who was licensed to kill. But as he matured, he was an obvious choice to play Bond perhaps like no actor since Connery. Brosnan took Bond into the new, post–Cold War world with style, but also with murderous determination: In GoldenEye , one of the best Bond movies, Brosnan looks directly into his best friend’s face and then drops him to his death. All of these men as Bond exuded a kind of energetic and masculine combination of professionalism and uncontrollable individuality. In the books, 007 is a complex character who soldiers on because it’s his job. He is sometimes morose and regretful. But all of that anguish would make for a drab series of movies, and to their credit, Connery, Lazenby, Moore, Brosnan, and even the dour Dalton manage to look they’re having fun—at least when they’re not about to be cut in half by lasers or strangled by a python. Here I will aggravate a lot of Bond fans: I think the series went off the rails with the casting of Daniel Craig and a drastic change in the 007 scripts. Instead of taking on supervillains, Bond tussled with terrorists and financiers, all while thinking and talking way too much about his psyche. Craig, another fine actor, was too brutish, and the scripts make plain that the job did, in fact, get to him. Craig’s Bond dressed well enough, but he always seemed uncomfortable in his suits: He’s a brawler with deep, complicated feelings, and one thing the cinematic James Bond does not need is a lot of feelings . The Craig scripts became like therapy sessions: When the big reveal came in the Craig movie Spectre— that the sadistic, megalomaniacal genius Ernst Blofeld was actually just a little boy with hurt feelings whose dad liked Jimmy Bond better when they were kids—I nearly walked out of the theater. (And by the way, what an utter waste of Christoph Waltz, who was born to play Blofeld.) By settling on Pattinson, who is even more angsty than Craig, the producers seem intent on continuing the decline. At least in the performances I’ve seen, Pattinson is sensitive ; he broods ; he’s conflicted ; he has messy hair; he has deep, watery eyes; he— He’s a walking young-Millennial stereotype, is what I’m saying. [ Read: Leave James Bond alone ] He doesn’t appear old or tough or coldly professional enough to be Bond. Think of this: Connery was 31 when he filmed Dr. No and 32 in From Russia With Love . Moore was 44 in Live and Let Die . Dalton was 41 when he strapped on his Walther PPK. Craig was 37 when he sat at the card table in Casino Royale . Pattinson is 40—and yet all of these guys look self-assured and old enough to play Pattinson’s father, not his colleague. (Even Brosnan seems like a tougher old brother, not a fellow Double-O.) Having most recently watched Pattinson mumble and anguish his way through The Batman , I cannot imagine him driving a Soviet tank through the streets of Russia, lecturing M on the finer points of blending cognac, or gently pushing the bad guy out of a space station’s airlock with an invitation to “take a giant step for mankind.” Perhaps the next film will do wonders; Moore, for one, was usually better when the scripts stuck to action instead of cheap comedy. But I have no faith, after the Craig psychodramas, that the writers will rescue Pattinson—or Bond. Amazon MGM is trying hard to work up a new image for Pattinson. Their first look has him in a tux sighting a sniper rifle, his face half-shadowed and his hair (for once) combed. Maybe it’ll work. But I still cannot imagine him trading barbs with the likes of Goldfinger: I imagine that when the mad criminal offers him a mint julep, Pattinson will scowl and explain that alcohol and sugar are bad for you.

items.title: Bourses scolaires 2026: la commission nationale d’attribution en session
items.description: Le ministère de l’enseignement secondaire, de la formation professionnelle et technique organise du 16 au 19 novembre 2026 à Koudougou, la session de la commission nationale d’attribution des bourses scolaires. A l’issue des travaux, plus de 34 000 bourses seront attribuées pour un montant global de 5 milliards F CFA. Les membres de la commission nationale d’attribution des bourses scolaires sont réunis du 16 au 19 novembre 2026 dans la cité du Cavalier rouge pour analyser les dossiers de demandes de bourses scolaires 2026. Le Ministre de l’Enseignement secondaire et de la Formation professionnelle et technique (MESFPT), Moumouni Zoungrana, a présidé l’ouverture des travaux de la session, avec à ses côtés le gouverneur de la région de Nando, Adama Jean Yves Béré. Le patron du département a indiqué que trois types de bourses vont être octroyés cette année, grâce aux réformes entreprises conformément aux idéaux de la Révolution progressiste populaire (RPP). Il s’agit de la bourse d’excellence, la bourse ordinaire et la bourse spécifique. « La bourse d’excellence, que nous sommes en train d’opérationnaliser progressivement, ne con-cerne pas seulement l’excellence à l’école. Elle prend en compte l’excellence dans tout autre domaine comme le sport, l’excellence dans le domaine de la culture et autres », a précisé Moumouni Zoungrana. Quant à la bourse spécifique, elle sera attribuée en tenant compte de critères de vulnérabilité tels que le handicap, l’orphelinat ou toute autre situation liée au déplacement des parents ou à un environnement défavorable. Il y a aussi la bourse intermédiaire, dont les bénéficiaires sont issus des classes intermédiaires. « La bourse ordinaire existait, mais le changement majeur, c’est le fait que nous avons retiré la pièce relative aux revenus des parents, parce que cette pièce était source d’injustice et de manipulation. C’est pourquoi, nous l’avons retirée pour donner la chance à tous les enfants », a-t-il ajouté. Le paiement des bourses par Mobile money et la digitalisation des dossiers de demandes de bourses sont les autres innovations. De l’avis du patron du département en charge de l’enseignement secondaire, ce sont au total 34 395 bourses qui vont être octroyées, pour une enveloppe financière qui tourne autour de 5 milliards F CFA. « Analyser tous les dossiers » Il a demandé aux membres de la commission nationale d’examiner les dossiers en ayant pour seule boussole les critères définis par le nouvel arrêté relatif aux bourses scolaires. Selon le Directeur général (DG) des appuis spécifiques au MESFPT, Boureima Nabaloum, la commission nationale est composée de membres issus de plusieurs départements ministériels, y compris la Primature. Il a fait savoir qu’après la collecte des candidatures, l’analyse et le traitement des dossiers par le secrétariat technique, conformément aux critères d’attribution des bourses définis, la commission a pour mission de valider les résultats provisoires. « Cela, en procédant à un réexamen de tous les dossiers pour s’assurer que le travail du secrétariat a été fait dans le respect des textes », a-t-il souligné. Boureima Nabaloum a rassuré qu’il est prévu des réclamations pour ceux qui estiment avoir été lésés. Après examen, si l’on constate qu’ils ont raison, la DGAS les rétablira dans leurs droits et un arrêté additionnel sera pris à cet effet. Des dispositions sont prises pour permettre à ceux pour qui l’opération a été effectuée, mais qui n’ont pas reçu l’argent, de faire des réclamations à partir de leur établissement d’origine, à travers les directions provinciales et régionales. Pour le directeur régional de l’enseignement secondaire de Nando, Hyacinthe Yaméogo, la tenue de la session de la commission nationale était très attendue parce qu’elle va permettre à de nombreux enfants de poursuivre leur cursus sans difficultés et soulager la souffrance des parents d’élèves. Beyon Romain NEBIE beynebie@gmail.com

items.title: Two suspects remanded over murder of 39-year-old woman in Oti Region
items.description: Two men have been remanded into prison custody by the Dambai Magistrate Court for their alleged involvement in the murder of a 39-year-old woman, Madam Rejoice Sena Akpaku, whose body was discovered in a bush near Adumadum in the Krachi East Municipality of the Oti Region. The suspects, identified as Isaac Sekyi, 36, and Reindolf Sekeni, 45, were arraigned on November 12 in a court presided over by Mr Alhassan Dramani and remanded to reappear on December 2, 2026. According to a police statement issued by Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP), Mr John Nchor, Oti Regional Public Affairs Officer, the deceased reportedly travelled from Somanya in the Eastern Region to Dormaa in the Oti Region on October 28, 2026, to retrieve GH¢19,000 allegedly owed to her by Sekyi. She, however, failed to return, prompting concerns about her whereabouts and subsequent police investigations into her disappearance. The statement said that following Sekyi’s arrest on November 10, 2026, police investigations led to the recovery of the deceased’s Infinix Smart 8 mobile phone from a chain of individuals linked to him. Investigators reportedly traced the phone to his girlfriend, Madam Seraphine Aku Koumah, who told the police that Sekyi had given it to her before she handed it over to his brother, Frank Sekyi. The mobile phone was subsequently retrieved and found to have been flashed, with its SIM card removed. A mobile phone technician, identified as Mr Mohammed Ali, was also arrested to assist with investigations. The police statement further disclosed that on November 11, 2026, Mr Sekyi allegedly confessed to the murder and implicated Mr Sekeni as an accomplice. He subsequently led police investigators to the location where the body had been concealed, where it was identified by a sibling of the deceased. A stick suspected to have been used in the attack was also retrieved from the scene and retained as an exhibit to support ongoing investigations. The police said they subsequently arraigned and remanded the two principal suspects into custody, while granting three other persons arrested in connection with the case police enquiry bail to assist with investigations. The Ghana Police Service assured the public it would investigate the matter professionally and in accordance with due process.

items.title: Photos from Day 1-3: Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair 2026
items.description: The Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair 2026 brought together three days of business exhibitions, product displays, shopping bargains, networking and live entertainment at Ghud Park, Accra Mall, from November 13 to 15. – Day 1 – Friday, November 13: The fair opened with more than 80 businesses showcasing products and services across food and beverages, fashion, beauty, agriculture, technology, electronics and household products. Joy Prime’s KMJ and content creator Quecy Official engaged exhibitors and patrons, while Nkyimkyim Band provided musical entertainment. – Day 2 – Saturday, November 14: Business exhibitions and shopping continued, with Ghanaian music duo Lali X Lola and King Jerry delivering energetic performances. Patrons sang and danced, while some vendors even carried their products onto the dance floor, creating an exciting blend of business and entertainment. – Day 3 – Sunday, November 15: The final day attracted shoppers seeking last-minute bargains, product discoveries and business connections. The Kekeli Borborbor Group and Shakers Band added cultural and musical excitement, bringing the three-day exhibition to a colourful close. The fair featured more than 80 brands, including Ecobank, MTN, GEPA, Glico Life and numerous Ghanaian SMEs showcasing locally made foods, beverages, clothing, cosmetics, agricultural products, technology and household essentials. Organised by the Multimedia Group in partnership with Ecobank and powered by JoyPrime, the event provided SMEs with opportunities to increase brand visibility, attract customers, generate sales and establish business partnerships. It ended as a vibrant celebration of Ghanaian entrepreneurship, creativity and innovation, successfully combining commerce, networking, shopping and entertainment. items.title: Mediaş : Do Pascal Sessouma s’est éteint à 69 ans
items.description: Le journaliste, enseignant et homme politique, Do Pascal Kiemdoro Sessouma, plus connu sous le pseudonyme de DPS, est décédé dans la nuit du samedi 14 au dimanche 15 novembre 2026, à Montréal, au Canada, à l’âge de 69 ans. Le monde des médias burkinabè est en deuil. Le journaliste, enseignant et homme politique, Do Pascal Kiemdoro Sessouma, est décédé dans la nuit du samedi 14 au dimanche 15 novembre 2026, à Montréal, au Canada, à l’âge de 69 ans. L’annonce de sa disparition a été faite par la Radiodiffusion télévision du Burkina (RTB), au cours de son journal télévisé de 13 heures du lundi 16 novembre. Né en 1957 à N’Dorola, Do Pascal Sessouma laisse derrière lui un parcours professionnel riche et diversifié, marqué par son engagement en faveur du journalisme et de la formation des jeunes générations. Figure bien connue du paysage médiatique burkinabè, il a effectué plusieurs passages remarqués à la RTB, où il a exercé les fonctions de journaliste-présentateur, de grand reporter et de rédacteur en chef. Il y a travaillé de 1981 à 1984, puis de 1997 à 2001. Son expérience professionnelle l’a également conduit au Canada, où il a exercé comme journaliste et grand reporter à Télé-Québec, de 1989 à 1996. Dans le cadre de l’émission « Nord-Sud », consacrée aux questions de développement international, il a parcouru plusieurs pays d’Afrique, d’Amérique, d’Asie et d’Europe, donnant ainsi une dimension internationale à son expérience journalistique. Au fil de sa carrière, il a également apporté son concours à la promotion de la liberté de la presse et de la démocratie, notamment en qualité de consultant auprès du Réseau Liberté, un organisme canadien intervenant en Afrique et dans les Caraïbes, entre 2004 et 2006. Au-delà de sa carrière de journaliste, Do Pascal Sessouma était également animé par la volonté de transmettre son savoir. De 2006 à 2010, il a enseigné le journalisme et la communication à l’Institut des sciences et techniques de l’information et de la communication (ISTIC), contribuant ainsi à la formation de plusieurs générations de professionnels des médias. Il a aussi fondé et dirigé l’agence DPS Communication entre 2001 et 2004. Entre 2010 et 2017, il a occupé les fonctions de responsable de la communication de la Maîtrise d’ouvrage de l’aéroport de Donsin (MOAD), mettant son expertise au service d’un important projet de développement national. Do Pascal Sessouma s’était également investi dans la vie politique nationale. En 2020, il a fondé le parti Vision Burkina, sous la bannière duquel il a pris part à l’élection présidentielle de la même année. Avec sa disparition, le Burkina Faso perd un professionnel des médias dont le parcours aura été marqué par la diversité des expériences, l’ouverture sur le monde et la transmission du savoir. Soumaïla BONKOUNGOU

items.title: Affaire Camille Makosso : Que dit la loi ivoirienne sur les injures envers un président étranger ?
items.description: Les déclarations injurieuses et offensantes du pasteur ivoirien Camille Makosso à l’endroit du président du Faso, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, soulèvent la question de leur qualification au regard du droit ivoirien. Cette affaire intervient alors que le Burkina Faso a sollicité la coopération judiciaire de la Côte d’Ivoire concernant l’activiste. Les propos tenus par le pasteur et influenceur ivoirien Camille Makosso à l’endroit du président du Faso, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, continuent de susciter des interrogations sur leurs éventuelles conséquences judiciaires. Les propos vulgaires et offensantes formulés par le pasteur ivoirien à l'endroit du chef de l'État burkinabè sur Internet pourraient être examinées au regard des dispositions légales en vigueur en Côte d’Ivoire, pour peu que les autorités judiciaires ivoiriennes acceptent de jetter un coup d'oeil au dossier. En effet, le droit ivoirien prévoit des sanctions contre les offenses publiques visant un chef d’État étranger. L’article 265 du Code pénal ivoirien de 2019 dispose que toute personne qui offense publiquement un chef d’État ou de gouvernement étranger, dans les conditions prévues par la loi, encourt une peine d’emprisonnement de trois mois à deux ans et une amende comprise entre 300 000 et 3 millions de francs CFA. Le juge peut prononcer l’une de ces deux peines seulement. Cette disposition pourrait être évoquée dans l’analyse juridique des propos visant le chef de l’État burkinabè. Une demande de coopération judiciaire du Burkina Faso Cette affaire intervient dans un contexte où la justice burkinabè a engagé des démarches auprès des autorités ivoiriennes concernant Camille Makosso. Dans une mise au point publiée le 13 novembre 2026, le ministère burkinabè de la Justice et des Droits humains a précisé qu’aucun mandat d’arrêt international n’avait été émis contre le pasteur ivoirien. Ouagadougou a plutôt sollicité la coopération judiciaire de la Côte d’Ivoire afin que des poursuites soient engagées contre lui dans son pays de résidence. Le dossier évoqué par les autorités burkinabè s’inscrit dans le cadre de procédures judiciaires portant notamment sur des faits présumés d’apologie du terrorisme et de complicité d’association de malfaiteurs terroristes. L’article Affaire Camille Makosso : Que dit la loi ivoirienne sur les injures envers un président étranger ? est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Burkina Faso : 354 agents du ministère de la Santé sommés de régulariser leur situation administrative
items.description: Le ministère de la Santé a mis en demeure 354 agents de rejoindre leur poste de travail ou de régulariser leur situation administrative. Dans un communiqué officiel, les intéressés disposent d’un délai de dix jours pour se présenter à la Direction des ressources humaines (DRH), sous peine de sanctions disciplinaires pouvant aller jusqu’à l’application des dispositions relatives à l’abandon de poste. Le ministère de la Santé passe à l’offensive contre les absences irrégulières au sein de son personnel. Au total, 354 agents sont concernés par une mise en demeure les invitant à se présenter à la Direction des ressources humaines afin de régulariser leur situation administrative. D’après un communiqué signé par la Direction de la communication et des relations publiques du ministère de la Santé (DCRP/MS), les agents concernés ne se seraient pas présentés à leur lieu de travail après l’expiration de leur période de disponibilité, de stage ou de toute autre position administrative, conformément aux actes administratifs les concernant. Le ministère précise toutefois que cette situation est constatée « sauf erreur ou omission de l'administration ». Dix jours pour se mettre en règle Pour régulariser leur situation, les 354 agents disposent d’un délai de dix jours à compter de la date de première diffusion du communiqué. Ils sont ainsi invités à se présenter impérativement à la Direction des ressources humaines du ministère. Cette démarche vise à permettre à l'administration de faire le point sur leur situation et de procéder, le cas échéant, aux régularisations nécessaires. Le ministère prévient cependant que le non-respect de cette mise en demeure pourrait entraîner des conséquences disciplinaires. Passé le délai fixé, les agents concernés s'exposent notamment à l'application des dispositions réglementaires relatives à l'absence irrégulière et à l'abandon de poste, sans préjudice des autres sanctions prévues par les textes en vigueur. À travers cette mesure, le département de la Santé entend rappeler à ses agents leurs obligations professionnelles et administratives, tout en invitant les personnes concernées à prendre les dispositions nécessaires dans les délais impartis.
